translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 125
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 125

sentences.zh: 【宋紀七】 起強圉大淵獻，盡上章攝提格，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Song Records 7] Beginning from Qiangyu Dayuanxian, ending at Shangzhang Shedige, altogether four years.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records, Part Seven] This section runs from the cyclical year Qiangyu Dayuanxian through Shangzhang Shedige — four years in all.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之下元嘉二十四年（

translations.literal: Middle and lower part of Emperor Taizu the Civil Emperor, twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia (
translations.idiomatic: The latter portion of the reign of Emperor Wen, founding emperor of Song — Yuanjia, year twenty-four (

sentences.zh: 丁亥，公元四四七年）

translations.literal: Dinghai, CE 447)
translations.idiomatic: dinghai year, 447 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲戌，大赦。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on jiaxu day, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the day jiaxu, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏吐京胡及山胡曹僕渾等反；

translations.literal: The Tujing Hu of Wei and the Shan Hu Cao Puhun and others rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: The Tujing Hu and the Shan Hu chieftain Cao Puhun rose in rebellion under Wei;

sentences.zh: 二月，征東將軍武昌王提等討平之。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Eastern Campaigning General, Prince Wu of Wuchang Ti and others suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Eastern Campaigning General Wuchang Wang Ti and others crushed the revolt.

sentences.zh: 癸未，魏主如中山。

translations.literal: On guiwei day, the Wei ruler went to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day, the Wei emperor traveled to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 魏師之克敦煌也，沮渠牧犍使人斫開府庫，取金玉及寶器，因不復閉。

translations.literal: When Wei forces conquered Dunhuang, Juqu Mujian had someone chop open the treasury, take gold, jade, and precious vessels, and therefore did not close it again.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei troops took Dunhuang, Juqu Mujian had his men break open the state treasury and carry off gold, jade, and precious vessels — and left the doors open.

sentences.zh: 小民爭入盜取之，有司索盜不獲。

translations.literal: Common people scrambled to enter and steal; the authorities sought the thieves but could not obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary folk rushed in to loot the storehouses, and officials could not recover what was stolen.

sentences.zh: 至是，牧犍所親及守藏者告之，且言牧犍父子多蓄毒藥，潛殺人前後以百數；

translations.literal: At this time, Mujian's intimates and the treasury keepers reported it, and moreover said that Mujian father and son had stored much poison and secretly killed people numbering over a hundred in all;
translations.idiomatic: Now his intimates and the keepers of the treasury denounced him, charging also that he and his sons had hoarded poisons and quietly murdered scores of people;

sentences.zh: 姊妹皆學左道。

translations.literal: His sisters all studied left-hand paths.
translations.idiomatic: His sisters had all practiced unlawful magic.

sentences.zh: 有司索牧犍家，得所匿物。

translations.literal: The authorities searched Mujian's household and obtained what had been concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials searched Mujian's residence and found the hidden goods.

sentences.zh: 魏主大怒，賜沮渠昭儀死，並誅其宗族，唯沮渠祖以先降得免。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler was greatly enraged, bestowed death on Juqu Zhaoyi, and executed his clan as well; only Juqu Zu, because he had surrendered earlier, was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor flew into a rage, ordered Lady Juqu to take her own life, and put her entire clan to death — only Juqu Zu was spared because he had surrendered earlier.

sentences.zh: 又有告牧犍猶與故臣民交通謀反者，三月，魏主遣崔浩就第賜牧犍死，謚曰哀王。

translations.literal: There were also those who reported that Mujian still maintained contact with former subjects plotting rebellion; in the third month, the Wei ruler sent Cui Hao to his residence to bestow death on Mujian, with posthumous title King Ai.
translations.idiomatic: When informers claimed Mujian was still plotting with his former subjects, the emperor sent Cui Hao in the third month to his house with orders that he die; his posthumous title was King Ai.

sentences.zh: 魏人徙定州丁零三千家於平城。

translations.literal: Wei people moved three thousand Dingling households of Dingzhou to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei relocated three thousand Dingling households from Dingzhou to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏西征諸將扶風公處真等八人，坐盜沒軍資及虜掠贓各千萬計，並斬之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, eight Wei generals of the western campaign including Fufeng Duke Chuzhen, on account of embezzling army supplies and booty plunder amounting to tens of millions each, were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, eight western campaign generals, among them Duke of Fufeng Chuzhen, were beheaded for embezzling army stores and loot worth tens of millions apiece.

sentences.zh: 初，上以貨重物輕，改鑄四銖錢。

translations.literal: Initially, because goods were costly and coin was light, the emperor changed the casting to four-zhu coin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because commodities were dear while coin was light in weight, the emperor had new four-zhu cash minted.

sentences.zh: 民多翦鑿古錢，取銅盜鑄。

translations.literal: The people largely clipped and chiseled old coin, took the copper, and illicitly cast.
translations.idiomatic: People widely clipped and filed down old coins, melted the copper, and cast counterfeit cash.

sentences.zh: 上患之。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed by this.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書事江夏王義恭建議，請以大錢一當兩。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Jiangxia Yigong proposed, requesting that large coin be valued one for two.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing Jiangxia Wang Yigong proposed that large coins be made to count as two standard coins each.

sentences.zh: 右僕射何尚之議曰：「夫泉貝之興，以估貨為本，事存交易，豈假多鑄！

translations.literal: Right Vice Director He Shangzhi argued, saying: "The rise of currency and shells rests on valuing goods as the foundation; the matter lies in exchange — how could one rely on excessive casting!
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director He Shangzhi objected: "Currency exists to measure the worth of goods; its purpose is trade — not to multiply the coinage!

sentences.zh: 數少則幣重，數多則物重，多少雖異，濟用不殊。

translations.literal: When the number is few, coin is heavy; when the number is many, goods are heavy — though the amounts differ, their utility in use is not different.
translations.idiomatic: Fewer coins make money dear; more coins make goods dear — the quantities differ, but the economy works the same either way.

sentences.zh: 況復以一當兩，徒崇虛價者邪？

translations.literal: Moreover, to make one count as two — is this not merely to exalt a false price?
translations.idiomatic: And to declare one coin worth two — would that not be nothing but inflating a fictitious value?

sentences.zh: 若今制遂行，富人之貲自倍，貧者彌增其困，懼非所以使之均壹也。」

translations.literal: If the present measure is carried through, the wealth of the rich will double of itself, while the poor will further increase their distress — I fear this is not the means to make things uniform."
translations.idiomatic: If this policy takes effect, the rich will see their assets double overnight while the poor grow poorer still — I doubt this is how to achieve fairness."

sentences.zh: 上卒從義恭議。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end followed Yigong's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor adopted Yigong's plan.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙未，徐州刺史衡陽文王義季卒。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, on yiwei day, Xuzhou Inspector Civil King of Hengyang Yiji died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, on the day yiwei, Xuzhou Inspector Hengyang Wen Wang Yiji died.

sentences.zh: 義季自彭城王義康之貶，遂縱酒不事事。

translations.literal: Since the demotion of Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, Yiji thereupon gave himself to drink and did not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Prince of Pengcheng Yikang's fall from grace, Yiji had drowned himself in wine and neglected all duties.

sentences.zh: 帝以書誚責，且戒之，義季猶酣飲自若，以至成疾而終。

translations.literal: The emperor with a letter reproached and admonished him, yet Yiji still drank freely as before, until he developed illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote to rebuke and warn him, but Yiji kept drinking as before until illness carried him off.

sentences.zh: 魏樂安宣王范卒。

translations.literal: Wei Prince Xuan of Le'an Fan died.
translations.idiomatic: Le'an Xuan Wang Fan of Wei died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬午，胡籓之子誕世殺豫章太守桓隆之，據郡反，欲奉前彭城王義康為主；

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on renwu day, Hu Fan's son Danshi killed Yuzhang Governor Huan Longzhi, seized the commandery and rebelled, wishing to install the former Prince of Pengcheng Yikang as leader;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day renwu, Hu Fan's son Danshi murdered Yuzhang governor Huan Longzhi, seized the commandery in revolt, and sought to set up the deposed Prince of Pengcheng Yikang as their leader;

sentences.zh: 前交州刺史檀和之去官歸，過豫章，擊斬之。

translations.literal: Former Jiaozhou Inspector Tan Hezhi, having left office and returned, passed through Yuzhang, attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Former Jiaozhou inspector Tan Hezhi, returning home after leaving office, passed through Yuzhang, attacked the rebels, and killed Danshi.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲寅，封皇子渾為汝陰王。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on jiayin day, the emperor's son Hun was enfeoffed as Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day jiayin, the emperor enfeoffed his son Hun as Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏晉王伏羅卒。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Wei Prince of Jin Fuluó died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Jin Wang Fuluó of Wei died.

sentences.zh: 楊文德據葭蘆城，招誘氐、羌，武都等五郡氐皆應之。

translations.literal: Yang Wende held Jialu City, recruited and enticed the Di and Qiang; the Di of five commanderies including Wudu all responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wende seized Jialu City and rallied the Di and Qiang; Di communities in five commanderies, including Wudu, all joined him.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之下元嘉二十五年（

translations.literal: Middle and lower part of Emperor Taizu the Civil Emperor, twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia (
translations.idiomatic: The latter portion of the reign of Emperor Wen — Yuanjia, year twenty-five (

sentences.zh: 戊子，公元四四八年）

translations.literal: Wuzi, CE 448)
translations.idiomatic: wuzi year, 448 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，魏仇池鎮將皮豹子帥諸軍擊之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, Wei Qiuchi garrison general Pi Baozi led the various armies to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Wei Qiuchi garrison commander Pi Baozi led his forces against him.

sentences.zh: 文德兵敗，棄城奔漢中。

translations.literal: Wende's army was defeated; he abandoned the city and fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wende's army was routed; he abandoned the city and fled to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 豹子收其妻子、僚屬、軍資及楊保宗所尚魏公主而還。

translations.literal: Baozi gathered his wife and children, staff, army supplies, and the Wei princess whom Yang Baozong had married, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi took captive Wende's family, his officials, military stores, and the Wei princess whom Yang Baozong had married, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，保宗將叛，公主勸之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Baozong was about to rebel, the princess urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Baozong was plotting defection, the princess had encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「奈何叛父母之國？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "How can you betray the country of your parents?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "How can you betray your parents' country?"

sentences.zh: 公主曰：「事成，為一國之母，豈比小縣公主哉！」

translations.literal: The princess said: "If the affair succeeds, I shall be mother of a state — how could that compare to being princess of a small county!"
translations.idiomatic: The princess replied: "If we succeed, I shall be queen mother of a realm — far better than being princess of some petty county!"

sentences.zh: 魏主賜之死。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler bestowed death on her.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor ordered her to die.

sentences.zh: 楊文德坐失守，免官，削爵土。

translations.literal: Yang Wende, on account of losing his hold, was dismissed from office and stripped of his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wende was stripped of office and deprived of his fief for losing his territory.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸卯，魏主如定州，罷塞圍役者；

translations.literal: Second month, on guimao day, the Wei ruler went to Dingzhou, dismissed those laboring on frontier fortifications;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day guimao, the Wei emperor went to Dingzhou and released men conscripted for frontier fortification work;

sentences.zh: 遂如上黨，誅潞縣叛民二千餘家，徙河西離石民五千餘家於平城。

translations.literal: thereupon went on to Shangdang, executed over two thousand rebel households of Lu County, and moved over five thousand households of Lishi in Hexi to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: then proceeded to Shangdang, executed more than two thousand rebel households in Lu County, and relocated over five thousand households from Lishi in Hexi to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己酉，帝大蒐於宣武場。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, on jiyou day, the emperor held a great hunt at Xuanwu Field.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the day jiyou, the emperor held a grand hunt at Xuanwu Field.

sentences.zh: 初，劉湛既誅，庾炳之遂見寵任，累遷吏部尚書，勢傾朝野。

translations.literal: Initially, after Liu Zhan was executed, Yu Bingzhi thereupon came to be favored and entrusted, was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing, and his power tilted court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Zhan's execution, Yu Bingzhi rose swiftly in favor, was promoted to Minister of Personnel, and came to dominate the court.

sentences.zh: 炳之無文學，性強急輕淺。

translations.literal: Bingzhi had no literary learning; by nature he was forceful, impatient, and shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi had no scholarly attainments and was by nature overbearing, impatient, and shallow.

sentences.zh: 既居選部，好詬詈賓客，且多納貨賂，士大夫皆惡之。

translations.literal: Once he held the Selection Bureau, he liked to revile guests and moreover took many bribes; scholar-officials all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in charge of appointments, he habitually abused visitors and took bribes freely; the gentry loathed him.

sentences.zh: 炳之留令史二人宿於私宅，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: Bingzhi kept two clerks lodging at his private residence; he was impeached by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi had two clerks stay overnight at his private residence and was reported by the censors.

sentences.zh: 上薄其過，欲不問。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded his offense lightly and wished not to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought the offense minor and was inclined to overlook it.

sentences.zh: 僕射何尚之因極陳炳之之短曰：「炳之見人有燭盤、佳驢，無不乞丐；

translations.literal: Vice Director He Shangzhi thereupon fully set forth Bingzhi's faults, saying: "Whenever Bingzhi saw someone with a candle stand or a fine donkey, he begged for it without exception;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director He Shangzhi pressed the case against Bingzhi at length: "Whenever Bingzhi saw a candle stand or a fine donkey in someone's possession, he begged for it;

sentences.zh: 選用不平，不可一二；

translations.literal: his selections and appointments were unfair — they cannot be numbered one or two;
translations.idiomatic: his appointments were corrupt beyond counting;

sentences.zh: 交結朋黨，構扇是非，亂俗傷風，過於范曄，所少，賊一事耳。

translations.literal: he formed factions and stirred up right and wrong, disordering custom and harming mores — exceeding Fan Ye; what he lacked was only the one matter of treason.
translations.idiomatic: he formed factions and stirred up trouble, corrupting public morals — worse than Fan Ye in every way except that he never committed outright treason.

sentences.zh: 縱不加罪，故宜出之。」

translations.literal: Even if he is not punished, he should still be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Even if you do not punish him, he should at least be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 上欲以炳之為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Bingzhi Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still meant to appoint Bingzhi governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 尚之曰：「炳之蹈罪負恩，方復有尹京赫赫之授，乃更成其形勢也。

translations.literal: Shangzhi said: "Bingzhi, having committed offense and betrayed favor, is now to receive again the illustrious appointment of governing the capital — this would only further complete his power.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi said: "Bingzhi has offended and betrayed your trust, yet you would give him the grand post of governing the capital — that would only swell his power further.

sentences.zh: 古人云：『無賞無罰，雖堯、舜不能為治。』

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'Without reward and without punishment, even Yao and Shun cannot govern.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: 'Without rewards and punishments, even Yao and Shun could not govern.'

sentences.zh: 臣昔啟范曄，亦懼犯顏，苟曰愚懷，九死不悔。

translations.literal: I formerly memorialized on Fan Ye, also fearing to offend your countenance; if I may speak my foolish mind, I would not regret dying nine times.
translations.idiomatic: When I spoke against Fan Ye before, I too feared your displeasure, but I would not shrink from speaking my mind even at the cost of my life.

sentences.zh: 歷觀古今，未有眾過藉藉，受貨數百萬，更得高官厚祿如炳之者也。」

translations.literal: Surveying past and present through the ages, there has never been one whose many offenses were notorious, who received bribes of millions, yet obtained high office and thick salary like Bingzhi."
translations.idiomatic: In all history I know of no man so notorious for misconduct, who took bribes in the millions, yet was rewarded with high office and rich emoluments as Bingzhi has been."

sentences.zh: 上乃免炳之官，以徐湛之為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon dismissed Bingzhi from office and made Xu Tanzhi Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then dismissed Bingzhi and appointed Xu Tanzhi governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 彭城太守王玄謨上言：「彭城要兼水陸，請以皇子撫臨州事。」

translations.literal: Pengcheng Governor Wang Xuanmo memorialized: "Pengcheng is strategic for both water and land routes; I request that an imperial prince oversee the province's affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng governor Wang Xuanmo memorialized: "Pengcheng commands both land and water routes; an imperial prince should be sent to oversee the province."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙卯，以武陵王駿為安北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on yimao day, Prince of Wuling Jun was made Northern Pacification General and Xuzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day yimao, Prince of Wuling Jun was appointed Northern Pacification General and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲戌，魏以交趾公韓拔為鄯善王，鎮鄯善，賦役其民，比之郡縣。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on jiaxu day, Wei made Duke of Jiaozhi Han Ba King of Shanshan, garrisoned Shanshan, levied and conscripted its people, comparing it to commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day jiaxu, Wei made Duke of Jiaozhi Han Ba king of Shanshan and stationed him there to tax and conscript the people on the same terms as a regular commandery.

sentences.zh: 當兩大錢行之經時，公私不以為便；

translations.literal: When the large coin valued at two had been in use for some time, public and private did not regard it as convenient;
translations.idiomatic: After the double-value large coins had been in circulation for some time, neither government nor people found them practical;

sentences.zh: 己卯，罷之。

translations.literal: on jimao day, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: on the day jimao they were abolished.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙寅，荊州刺史南譙王義宣進位司空。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on bingyin day, Jingzhou Inspector Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan was advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day bingyin, Jingzhou inspector Nanqiao Wang Yixuan was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，魏主如廣德宮。

translations.literal: On xinyou day, the Wei ruler went to Guangde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyou the Wei emperor went to Guangde Palace.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，甲子，封皇子彧為淮陽王。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, on jiazi day, the emperor's son Yu was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, on the day jiazi, the emperor enfeoffed his son Yu as Prince of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 西域般悅國去平城萬有餘里，遣使詣魏，請與魏東西合擊柔然。

translations.literal: The Western Region state of Banyue was over ten thousand li from Pingcheng; it sent envoys to Wei, requesting to join with Wei in a pincer attack on the Rouran from east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Banyue in the Western Regions, more than ten thousand li from Pingcheng, sent envoys to Wei proposing a joint east-west strike against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 魏主許之，中外戒嚴。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler assented; within and without, the realm was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor agreed, and the court and provinces were placed on war footing.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛未，以尚書右僕射何尚之為左僕射，領軍將軍沈演之為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on xinwei day, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi was made Left Vice Director; Commanding General Shen Yanzhi was made Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day xinwei, Right Vice Director He Shangzhi was promoted to Left Vice Director, and Commanding General Shen Yanzhi was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: On bingxu day, the Wei ruler went to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu the Wei emperor went to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 魏成周公萬度歸擊焉耆，大破之，焉耆王鳩屍卑那奔龜茲。

translations.literal: Wei Prince Cheng of Zhou Wandugui attacked Yanqi, routed it greatly; the King of Yanqi Jiushibina fled to Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Prince Cheng of Zhou Wandugui attacked Yanqi and routed it; King Jiushibina of Yanqi fled to Kucha.

sentences.zh: 魏主詔唐和與前部王車伊洛帥所部兵會度歸討西域。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered Tang He and Former-Department King Che Yiluo to lead their troops to join Wandugui in pacifying the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor ordered Tang He and Former-Department King Che Yiluo to bring their forces to join Wandugui in subduing the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 和說降柳驢等六城，因共擊波居羅城，拔之。

translations.literal: He persuaded Liulü and six other cities to surrender, and together they attacked Bojuluo City and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded six cities including Liulü to submit, then together they stormed and captured Bojuluo City.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛丑，魏弘農昭王奚斤卒，子它觀襲。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on xinchou day, Wei Prince Zhao of Hongnong Xi Jin died; his son Taguan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day xinchou, Hongnong Zhao Wang Xi Jin of Wei died; his son Taguan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「斤關西之敗，罪固當死；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said: "Jin's defeat in Guanxi — the crime truly deserved death;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said: "Jin's defeat in Guanxi deserved death;

sentences.zh: 朕以斤佐命先朝，復其爵邑，使得終天年，君臣之分亦足矣。」

translations.literal: I, because Jin aided the mandate in the former dynasty, restored his rank and fief, enabling him to complete his natural years — the distinction between ruler and minister is also sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: but because he had served the founding of our dynasty, I restored his rank and fief and let him live out his days — that is enough for the bond between sovereign and minister."

sentences.zh: 乃降它觀爵為公。

translations.literal: Thereupon Taguan's rank was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore reduced Taguan's title to duke.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On guihai day, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guihai Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏萬度歸自焉耆西討龜茲，留唐和鎮焉耆。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Wei Wandugui from Yanqi campaigned west against Kucha, leaving Tang He to garrison Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Wandugui marched west from Yanqi against Kucha, leaving Tang He to hold Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 柳驢戍主乙直伽謀叛，和擊斬之，由是諸胡鹹附，西域復平。

translations.literal: The garrison commander of Liulü, Yizhijia, plotted rebellion; He attacked and beheaded him; thereby all the Hu submitted, and the Western Regions were pacified again.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander of Liulü, Yizhijia, plotted rebellion; He attacked and killed him, and thereafter all the frontier peoples submitted and the Western Regions were pacified once more.

sentences.zh: 魏太子朝於行宮，遂從伐柔然。

translations.literal: The Wei crown prince attended court at the traveling palace, then followed in the campaign against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei crown prince paid his respects at the mobile palace, then accompanied the campaign against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 至受降城，不見柔然，因積糧於城內，置戍而還。

translations.literal: Reaching Shouxiang City, they did not see the Rouran; they therefore stored grain within the city, set a garrison, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Shouxiang City but found no Rouran; they stockpiled grain there, left a garrison, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之下元嘉二十六年（

translations.literal: Middle and lower part of Emperor Taizu the Civil Emperor, twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia (
translations.idiomatic: The latter portion of the reign of Emperor Wen — Yuanjia, year twenty-six (

sentences.zh: 己丑，公元四四九年）

translations.literal: Jichou, CE 449)
translations.idiomatic: jichou year, 449 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊辰朔，魏主饗群臣於漠南。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the new moon wuchen day, the Wei ruler feasted the ministers south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, wuchen, the Wei emperor feasted his ministers south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，復伐柔然。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day, he again campaigned against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu he launched another campaign against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 高涼王那出東道，略陽王羯兒出西道，魏主與太子出涿邪山，行數千里。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoliang Na marched by the eastern route, Prince of Lueyang Jie'er by the western route; the Wei ruler and the crown prince set out from Zhuoye Mountain and traveled several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoliang Wang Na took the eastern route and Lueyang Wang Jie'er the western; the emperor and crown prince advanced from Zhuoye Mountain and marched thousands of li.

sentences.zh: 柔然處羅可汗恐懼，遠遁。

translations.literal: The Rouran Chuluokehan was afraid and fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran khan Chuluokehan, terrified, fled deep into the steppe.

sentences.zh: 二月，己亥，上如丹徒，謁京陵。

translations.literal: Second month, on jihai day, the emperor went to Dantu and visited the capital tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day jihai, the emperor went to Dantu and paid his respects at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁巳，大赦。

translations.literal: Third month, on dingsi day, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day dingsi, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 募諸州樂移者數千家以實京口。

translations.literal: Several thousand households from the provinces who were willing to relocate were recruited to fill Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand households from the provinces who were willing to move were recruited to populate Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: On gengyin day, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，壬午，帝還建康。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, on renwu day, the emperor returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on the day renwu, the emperor returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: On gengyin day, the Wei ruler went to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin the Wei emperor went to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 帝欲經略中原，群臣爭獻策以迎合取寵。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to plan operations in the Central Plains; the ministers vied to present strategies to win favor by pleasing him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to recover the Central Plains, and his ministers competed to offer strategies that would win his favor.

sentences.zh: 彭城太守王玄謨尤好進言，帝謂侍臣曰：「觀玄謨所陳，令人有封狼居須意。」

translations.literal: Pengcheng Governor Wang Xuanmo was especially fond of advancing proposals; the emperor said to his attendant ministers: "Observing what Xuanmo has set forth, it makes one have the intent of fenglang juxu."
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng governor Wang Xuanmo was especially eager to offer plans for conquest; the emperor told his attendants, "Listening to Xuanmo, one feels the urge to plant a victory banner on Langjuxu Mountain."

sentences.zh: 御史中丞袁淑言於上曰：「陛下今當席捲趙、魏，檢玉岱宗；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Shu said to the emperor: "Your Majesty should now sweep up Zhao and Wei, inspect the jade at Mount Tai;
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Shu said to the throne, "Your Majesty is poised to sweep through Zhao and Wei and perform the jade rite at Mount Tai;

sentences.zh: 臣逢千載之會，願上封禪書。」

translations.literal: your servant meets the occasion of a thousand years and wishes to present a fengshan memorial."
translations.idiomatic: I have lived to see this once-in-a-millennium moment and beg leave to submit a memorial on the fengshan rites."

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 淑，耽之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Shu was the great-grandson of Danzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was the great-grandson of Danzhi.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛未，以廣陵王誕為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on xinwei day, Prince of Guangling Dan was made Yongzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day xinwei, Prince of Guangling Dan was appointed inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 上以襄陽外接關、河，欲廣其資力，乃罷江州軍府，文武悉配雍州；

translations.literal: The emperor, because Xiangyang bordered Guan and the Yellow River, wished to expand its resources; he therefore abolished the Jiangzhou military headquarters, and civil and military officials were all assigned to Yongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiangyang lay on the frontier facing Guan and the Yellow River, the emperor sought to strengthen it: he abolished the Jiangzhou military headquarters and transferred all its civil and military staff to Yongzhou;

sentences.zh: 湘州入台租稅，悉給襄陽。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou's taxes remitted to the capital were all given to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: and directed all Xiangzhou tax revenues destined for the capital to Xiangyang instead.

sentences.zh: 九月，魏主伐柔然。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the Wei ruler campaigned against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Wei emperor campaigned against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 高涼王那出東道，略陽王羯兒出中道。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoliang Na marched by the eastern route, Prince of Lueyang Jie'er by the central route.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoliang Wang Na took the eastern route and Lueyang Wang Jie'er the central route.

sentences.zh: 柔然處羅可汗悉國中精兵圍那數十里；

translations.literal: The Rouran Chuluokehan gathered all the elite troops of the state and surrounded Na for several tens of li;
translations.idiomatic: Rouran khan Chuluokehan mustered the kingdom's best troops and surrounded Na for dozens of li;

sentences.zh: 那掘塹堅守，相持數日。

translations.literal: Na dug trenches and held firm; they faced off for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Na dug trenches and held his ground; the standoff lasted several days.

sentences.zh: 處羅數挑戰，輒為那所敗。

translations.literal: Chuluo repeatedly offered battle and was each time defeated by Na.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo challenged him repeatedly and was beaten back each time.

sentences.zh: 以那眾少而堅，疑大軍將至，解圍夜去。

translations.literal: Because Na's force was few yet firm, he suspected a great army was about to arrive, lifted the siege, and left by night.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Na's small but stubborn force, he feared a larger army was coming, broke the siege, and withdrew under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 那引兵追之，九日九夜。

translations.literal: Na led troops in pursuit for nine days and nine nights.
translations.idiomatic: Na pursued for nine days and nine nights.

sentences.zh: 處羅益懼，棄輜重，逾穹隆嶺遠遁。

translations.literal: Chuluo grew still more afraid, abandoned baggage, crossed Qionglong Ridge, and fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo grew more terrified, abandoned his baggage train, crossed Qionglong Ridge, and fled deep into the steppe.

sentences.zh: 那收其輜重，引軍還，與魏主會於廣澤。

translations.literal: Na gathered his baggage and led the army back, joining the Wei ruler at Guangze.
translations.idiomatic: Na seized the abandoned baggage and withdrew to join the Wei emperor at Guangze.

sentences.zh: 略陽王羯兒收柔然民畜凡百餘萬。

translations.literal: Prince of Lueyang Jie'er gathered Rouran people and livestock totaling over a million.
translations.idiomatic: Lueyang Wang Jie'er captured more than a million Rouran people and livestock.

sentences.zh: 自是柔然衰弱，屏跡不敢犯魏塞。

translations.literal: From this time the Rouran weakened; they withdrew and did not dare violate Wei's frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Rouran were enfeebled and dared not raid Wei's borders again.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，戊申，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, on wushen day, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the twelfth month, on the day wushen, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 沔北諸山蠻寇雍州，建威將軍沈慶之帥後軍中兵參軍柳元景、隨郡太守宗愨等二萬人討之，八道俱進。

translations.literal: The mountain barbarians north of the Han raided Yongzhou; Establishing Might General Shen Qingzhi led Rear Army Central Troops Staff Officer Liu Yuanjing, Suixiang Governor Zong Que, and others — twenty thousand men — to suppress them, advancing on eight routes together.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain tribes north of the Han raided Yongzhou; Establishing Might General Shen Qingzhi led twenty thousand men under Rear Army staff officer Liu Yuanjing and Suixiang governor Zong Que against them, advancing on eight fronts at once.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸將討蠻者皆營於山下以迫之，蠻得據山發矢石以擊，官軍多不利。

translations.literal: Previously, generals who campaigned against the barbarians all encamped below the mountains to press them; the barbarians could hold the heights and launch arrows and stones, and government troops often fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier commanders had always camped below the mountains to hem the tribes in, allowing them to hold the heights and rain down missiles — with poor results for the government forces.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「去歲蠻田大稔，積穀重巖，不可與之曠日相守也。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "Last year the barbarians' fields yielded greatly; they have stored grain in layered cliffs — we cannot contend with them in a prolonged standoff.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "Last year the tribes harvested abundantly and have grain stored in their cliff strongholds — we cannot afford a long siege.

sentences.zh: 不若出其不意，沖其腹心，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: Better to take them unawares and strike their vital center — we are certain to break them."
translations.idiomatic: Better to take them by surprise and strike at their heart — we are sure to break them."

sentences.zh: 乃命諸軍斬木登山，鼓噪而前，群蠻震恐。

translations.literal: He then ordered the armies to cut trees and climb the mountains, advancing with drums and shouts; the barbarian masses were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his troops to cut timber, climb the heights, and advance with drums and war cries; the tribes were terrified.

sentences.zh: 因其恐而擊之，所向奔潰。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of their fear, he struck them; wherever he went they fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: He struck while they were panicked, and they broke and fled wherever he turned.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝中之下元嘉二十七年（

translations.literal: Middle and lower part of Emperor Taizu the Civil Emperor, twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia (
translations.idiomatic: The latter portion of the reign of Emperor Wen — Yuanjia, year twenty-seven (

sentences.zh: 庚寅，公元四五零年）

translations.literal: Gengyin, CE 450)
translations.idiomatic: gengyin year, 450 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉，魏主如洛陽。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on yiyou day, the Wei ruler went to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the day yiyou, the Wei emperor went to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 沈慶之自冬至春，屢破雍州蠻。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi from winter through spring repeatedly defeated the Yongzhou barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: From winter through spring Shen Qingzhi repeatedly defeated the Yongzhou tribes.

sentences.zh: 因蠻所聚谷以充軍食，前後斬首三千級，虜二萬八千餘口，降者二萬五千餘戶。

translations.literal: Using grain the barbarians had gathered to supply army provisions, he cut off heads numbering three thousand in all, captured over twenty-eight thousand persons, and received the surrender of over twenty-five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He fed his army on grain the tribes had stockpiled, took three thousand heads in all, captured more than twenty-eight thousand people, and received the surrender of over twenty-five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 幸諸山大羊蠻憑險築城，守禦甚固。

translations.literal: The Dayang barbarians of Xingzhu Mountain relied on perilous terrain and built a city; their defense was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: The Dayang tribe of Xingzhu Mountain held a fortified city in rugged terrain and defended it stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 慶之擊之，命諸軍連營於山中，開門相通，各穿池於營內，朝夕不外汲。

translations.literal: Qingzhi attacked them, ordering the armies to link camps in the mountains with gates connecting one to another, each digging pools within the camp so that morning and evening they need not go outside to draw water.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi besieged them, linking camps through the mountains with connecting gates and digging pools inside each camp so his men never had to leave for water.

sentences.zh: 頃之，風甚，蠻潛兵夜來燒營。

translations.literal: Shortly after, the wind was fierce; the barbarians sent troops by night to burn the camps.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a strong wind arose, and the tribes sent men by night to set the camps ablaze.

sentences.zh: 諸軍以池水沃火，多出弓弩夾射之，蠻兵散走。

translations.literal: The armies doused the fire with pool water, sent out many crossbows to shoot from both sides, and the barbarian troops scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The troops doused the flames with their pool water and raked the attackers with crossbow fire from both sides; the tribal warriors scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 蠻所據險固，不可攻，慶之乃置六戍以守之。

translations.literal: The perilous ground the barbarians held could not be attacked; Qingzhi therefore set six garrisons to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: The stronghold was too rugged to storm, so Qingzhi established six garrisons to blockade it.

sentences.zh: 久之，蠻食盡，稍稍請降；

translations.literal: After a long time the barbarians' food was exhausted and they gradually requested surrender;
translations.idiomatic: After a long siege the tribes ran out of food and gradually asked to surrender;

sentences.zh: 悉遷於建康以為營戶。

translations.literal: all were moved to Jiankang to serve as camp households.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi relocated them all to Jiankang as military settler households.

sentences.zh: 魏主將入寇。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler was about to invade.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor prepared to invade the south.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲午，大獵於梁川。

translations.literal: Second month, on jiawu day, a great hunt at Liangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day jiawu, he held a grand hunt at Liangchuan.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，敕淮、泗諸郡：「若魏寇小至，則各堅守；

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and ordered the Huai and Si commanderies: "If the Wei invaders come in small force, each shall hold firm;
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, the Song emperor ordered the Huai and Si commanderies: "If the Wei come in small numbers, hold your ground;

sentences.zh: 大至，則拔民歸壽陽。」

translations.literal: if they come in great force, then withdraw the people to Shouyang."
translations.idiomatic: if they come in force, evacuate the populace to Shouyang."

sentences.zh: 邊戍偵候不明，辛亥，魏主自將步騎十萬奄至。

translations.literal: The frontier garrisons' scouting was unclear; on xinhai day the Wei ruler personally led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry and arrived suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier scouts failed to give warning; on the day xinhai the Wei emperor personally led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry in a surprise descent.

sentences.zh: 南頓太守鄭琨、穎川太守郭道隱並棄城走。

translations.literal: Nandun Governor Zheng Kun and Yingchuan Governor Guo Daoyin both abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Nandun governor Zheng Kun and Yingchuan governor Guo Daoyin both abandoned their cities and fled.

sentences.zh: 是時，豫州刺史南平王鑠鎮壽陽，遣左軍行參軍陳憲行汝南郡事，守懸瓠，城中戰士不滿千人，魏主圍之。

translations.literal: At this time, Yuzhou Inspector Prince of Nanping Shuo was stationed at Shouyang; he sent Left Army Acting Staff Officer Chen Xian to administer Runan commandery affairs and hold Xuanchi — warriors in the city numbered fewer than a thousand; the Wei ruler besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou inspector Nanping Wang Shuo was then at Shouyang; he sent Left Army acting staff officer Chen Xian to govern Runan and hold Xuanchi with fewer than a thousand defenders. The Wei emperor besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 三月，以軍興，減內外百官俸三分之一。

translations.literal: Third month, because of military mobilization, salaries of inner and outer officials were reduced by one third.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, because of the war, court and provincial officials' salaries were cut by one third.

sentences.zh: 魏人晝夜攻懸瓠，多作高樓，臨城以射之，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: The Wei people attacked Xuanchi day and night, building many tall towers overlooking the city to shoot at it; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei attacked Xuanchi day and night, erecting tall siege towers to rain arrows on the defenders.

sentences.zh: 城中負戶以汲，施大鉤於沖車之端以牽樓堞，壞其南城。

translations.literal: Within the city they carried door panels to draw water; they fitted great hooks on the ends of battering rams to pull down tower parapets and destroyed the southern wall.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders used door panels as shields to fetch water and fixed great hooks on battering rams to tear down the enemy towers, breaching the southern wall.

sentences.zh: 陳憲內設女牆，外立木柵以拒之。

translations.literal: Chen Xian set up parapets within and erected wooden palisades without to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xian built inner parapets and outer wooden palisades to hold the breach.

sentences.zh: 魏人填塹，肉薄登城，憲督厲將士苦戰，積屍與城等。

translations.literal: The Wei filled the moat and pressed close to scale the wall; Xian directed and urged the officers and soldiers in bitter fighting until heaped corpses were level with the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei filled the moat and pressed the assault; Xian drove his men in desperate fighting until corpses piled level with the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 魏人乘屍上城。

translations.literal: The Wei climbed the wall on the corpses.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei climbed the wall on the bodies of the dead.

sentences.zh: 短兵相接，憲銳氣愈奮，戰士無不一當百，殺傷萬計，城中死者亦過半。

translations.literal: At close quarters they joined battle; Xian's fighting spirit grew still keener; warriors were each as one against a hundred; casualties numbered in the tens of thousands, and dead within the city also exceeded half.
translations.idiomatic: In hand-to-hand combat Xian's spirit only sharpened; each defender fought as ten; tens of thousands fell, and more than half the garrison perished.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣永昌王仁將步騎萬餘，驅所掠六郡生口北屯汝陽。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler sent Prince Yongchang Ren with over ten thousand infantry and cavalry to drive the captives seized from six commanderies north to camp at Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent Yongchang Wang Ren with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to drive captives from six commanderies north to camp at Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 時徐州刺史武陵王駿鎮彭城，帝遣間使命駿發騎，繼三日糧襲之。

translations.literal: At this time Xuzhou Inspector Prince of Wuling Jun was stationed at Pengcheng; the emperor sent a secret envoy ordering Jun to dispatch cavalry with three days' provisions to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou inspector Wuling Wang Jun was then at Pengcheng; the emperor sent a secret envoy ordering him to dispatch cavalry with three days' rations for a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 駿發百里內馬得千五百匹，分為五軍，遣參軍劉泰之帥安北騎兵行參軍垣謙之、田曹行參軍臧肇之、集曹行參軍尹定、武陵左常侍杜幼文、殿中將軍程天祚等將之，直趨汝陽。

translations.literal: Jun raised horses within a hundred li and obtained fifteen hundred, divided them into five armies, and sent Staff Officer Liu Taizhi to lead Northern Pacification Cavalry Acting Staff Officer Yuan Qianzhi, Agriculture Bureau Acting Staff Officer Zang Zhaozhi, Assembly Bureau Acting Staff Officer Yin Ding, Wuling Left Regular Attendant Du Youwen, Palace General Cheng Tianzuo, and others to command them, heading straight for Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun mustered fifteen hundred horses from within a hundred li, divided them into five columns, and sent staff officer Liu Taizhi at the head of Northern Pacification cavalry acting staff officer Yuan Qianzhi, agriculture bureau staff officer Zang Zhaozhi, assembly bureau staff officer Yin Ding, Wuling left regular attendant Du Youwen, and palace general Cheng Tianzuo straight for Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 魏人唯虎救兵自壽陽來，不備彭城。

translations.literal: The Wei people expected only Tiger's relief troops from Shouyang and were not prepared for Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei expected only relief from Shouyang and were unprepared for an attack from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，泰之等潛進擊之，殺三千餘人，燒其輜重，魏人奔散，諸生口悉得東走。

translations.literal: On dingyou day, Taizhi and the others advanced secretly and struck them, killing over three thousand, burning their baggage, the Wei scattered in flight, and all the captives were able to flee east.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, Taizhi's force struck by surprise, killed more than three thousand, burned the baggage train, and routed the Wei; all the captives escaped eastward.

sentences.zh: 魏人偵知泰之等兵無後繼，復引兵擊之。

translations.literal: The Wei scouts learned that Taizhi's troops had no follow-on force and again led troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei scouts discovered that Taizhi had no reinforcements and turned to counterattack.

sentences.zh: 垣謙之先退，士卒驚亂，棄仗走。

translations.literal: Yuan Qianzhi withdrew first; soldiers were alarmed and disordered, cast aside weapons, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianzhi retreated first; the troops panicked, threw down their weapons, and fled.

sentences.zh: 泰之為魏人所殺，肇之溺死，天祚為魏所擒，謙之、定、幼文及士卒免者九百餘人，馬還者四百匹。

translations.literal: Taizhi was killed by the Wei; Zhaozhi drowned; Tianzuo was captured by Wei; Qianzhi, Ding, Youwen, and soldiers who escaped numbered over nine hundred; horses that returned numbered four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhi was killed, Zhaozhi drowned, and Tianzuo was captured; Qianzhi, Ding, Youwen, and just over nine hundred men escaped, with four hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 魏主攻懸瓠四十二日，帝遣南平內史臧質詣壽陽，與安蠻司馬劉康祖共將兵救懸瓠。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler attacked Xuanchi for forty-two days; the emperor sent Nanping Interior Secretary Zang Zhi to Shouyang to join with Pacify the Barbarians Major Liu Kangzu in leading troops to relieve Xuanchi.
translations.idiomatic: After forty-two days of siege the emperor sent Nanping interior secretary Zang Zhi to Shouyang to join Pacify the Barbarians major Liu Kangzu in relieving Xuanchi.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣殿中尚書任城公乞地真逆拒之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler sent Palace Master of Writing, Prince of Rencheng Qidizhen to oppose and resist them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent palace master of writing Rencheng Duke Qidizhen to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 質等擊斬乞地真。

translations.literal: Zhi and the others attacked and beheaded Qidizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's force attacked and killed Qidizhen.

sentences.zh: 康祖，道錫之從兄也。

translations.literal: Kangzu was the elder cousin of Daoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu was the elder cousin of Daoxi.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，魏主引兵還。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, the Wei ruler led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the Wei emperor withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，至平城。

translations.literal: On guimao day, he reached Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao he reached Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 壬子，安北將軍武陵王駿降號鎮軍將軍，垣謙之伏誅，尹定、杜幼文付尚方；

translations.literal: On renzi day, Northern Pacification General Prince of Wuling Jun was reduced in rank to Suppressing Army General; Yuan Qianzhi was executed; Yin Ding and Du Youwen were handed over to the Palace Workshops;
translations.idiomatic: On the day renzi, Northern Pacification General Wuling Wang Jun was demoted to Suppressing Army General; Yuan Qianzhi was executed; Yin Ding and Du Youwen were handed to the palace workshops;

sentences.zh: 以陳憲為龍驤將軍、汝南、新蔡二郡太守。

translations.literal: Chen Xian was made Soaring Dragon General and Governor of the two commanderies Runan and Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: and Chen Xian was made Soaring Dragon General and governor of Runan and Xincai.

sentences.zh: 魏主遺帝書曰：「前蓋吳反逆，扇動關、隴。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler sent the emperor a letter, saying: "Formerly that Wu rebel stirred up Guan and Long.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent the Song emperor a letter: "Formerly that Wu rebel stirred up Guan and Long.

sentences.zh: 彼復使人就而誘之，丈夫遺以弓矢，婦人遺以環釧；

translations.literal: He again sent men to go and entice them, giving men bows and arrows, giving women rings and bracelets;
translations.idiomatic: You sent agents to entice them — bows and arrows for the men, rings and bracelets for the women;

sentences.zh: 是曹正欲譎誑取賂，豈有遠相服從之理！

translations.literal: this was Cao's intent to deceive and cheat for bribes — how could there be reason for distant submission!
translations.idiomatic: Cao merely meant to trick and bribe them — as if they would submit to you from afar!

sentences.zh: 為大丈夫，何不自來取之，而以貨誘我邊民？

translations.literal: As a great man, why not come yourself to take them, yet use goods to entice my frontier people?
translations.idiomatic: If you are a true man, why not come yourself and take them, instead of bribing my border people?

sentences.zh: 募往者復除七年，是賞奸也。

translations.literal: Recruiting those who went and exempting them for seven years — this is rewarding treachery.
translations.idiomatic: You recruit defectors and exempt them seven years from tax — you reward treachery.

sentences.zh: 我今來至此土所得多少，孰與彼前後得我民邪？

translations.literal: I have now come to this land — how much have I obtained, compared with how many of my people he obtained before and after?
translations.idiomatic: How many of your people have I taken on this campaign, compared with how many of mine you have lured away over the years?

sentences.zh: 「彼若欲存劉氏血食者，當割江以北輸之，攝守南渡。

translations.literal: " If he wishes to preserve the Liu clan's blood offerings, he should cede north of the Yangzi and deliver it, withdraw and guard the southern crossing.
translations.idiomatic: " If you wish the Liu house to survive, cede everything north of the Yangzi and withdraw south of the river.

sentences.zh: 如此，當釋江南使彼居之。

translations.literal: If so, I shall release Jiangnan for him to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Do so, and I will leave the south for you to inhabit.

sentences.zh: 不然，可善敕方鎮、剌史、守宰嚴供帳之具，來秋當往取揚州。

translations.literal: Otherwise, he may well order regional commanders, inspectors, and magistrates to prepare provisions and equipment strictly — next autumn I shall go take Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, tell your regional commanders, inspectors, and magistrates to prepare supplies in earnest — next autumn I shall come for Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 大勢已至，終不相縱。

translations.literal: The great momentum has arrived; in the end I will not spare him.
translations.idiomatic: My power is upon you; I will show no mercy.

sentences.zh: 彼往日北通蠕蠕，西結赫連、沮渠、吐谷渾，東連馮私、高麗。

translations.literal: He formerly connected north with the Rouran, west allied with Helian, Juqu, and Tuyuhun, east linked with Fengsi and Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: You once allied north with the Rouran, west with Helian, Juqu, and Tuyuhun, east with Fengsi and Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 凡此數國，我皆滅之。

translations.literal: All these several states — I have destroyed them all.
translations.idiomatic: I have destroyed them all.

sentences.zh: 以此而觀，彼豈能獨立！

translations.literal: Viewed by this, how can he stand alone!
translations.idiomatic: Judging by that, how can you stand alone!

sentences.zh: 「蠕蠕吳提、吐賀真皆已死，我今北征，先除有足之寇。

translations.literal: " Rouran Wuti and Tuhezhen are both already dead; I now campaign north and first eliminate the foe with feet.
translations.idiomatic: " Rouran khans Wuti and Tuhezhen are both dead; I campaign north first against enemies who can fight on foot.

sentences.zh: 彼若不從命，來秋當復往取之；

translations.literal: If he does not obey, next autumn I shall again go take him;
translations.idiomatic: If you do not obey, next autumn I shall come for you again;

sentences.zh: 以彼無足，故不先討耳。

translations.literal: because he has no feet, I do not strike first.
translations.idiomatic: because you have no legs to stand on, I deal with you last.

sentences.zh: 我往之日，彼作何計，為握塹自守，為築垣以自障也？

translations.literal: On the day I go, what plan will he make — will he dig trenches and hold himself, or build walls to screen himself?
translations.idiomatic: When I come, what will you do — dig trenches and hide, or build walls to cower behind?

sentences.zh: 我當顯然往取揚州，不若彼翳行竊步也。

translations.literal: I shall openly go take Yangzhou — not like his secret creeping steps.
translations.idiomatic: I shall march openly on Yangzhou — not skulk about like a thief as you do.

sentences.zh: 彼來偵諜，我已擒之，復縱還。

translations.literal: His scouts who came — I have already captured them and again released them.
translations.idiomatic: I captured your spies and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 其人目所盡見，委曲善問之。

translations.literal: Let the man question them fully on all he saw with his own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Ask them yourself what they saw.

sentences.zh: 「彼前使裴方明取仇池，既得之，疾其勇功，已不能容；

translations.literal: " He formerly sent Pei Fangming to take Qiuchi; once he obtained it, he resented his brave achievement and could not tolerate him;
translations.idiomatic: " You sent Pei Fangming to take Qiuchi; once he succeeded, you envied his valor and could not abide him;

sentences.zh: 有臣如此尚殺之，烏得與我校邪！

translations.literal: having such a minister yet killing him — how can he match wits with me!
translations.idiomatic: you kill men like that — how can you hope to match me!

sentences.zh: 彼非我敵也。

translations.literal: He is not my match.
translations.idiomatic: You are no match for me.

sentences.zh: 彼常欲與我一交戰，我亦不癡，復非苻堅，何時與彼交戰？

translations.literal: He always wishes to join battle with me once; I am not foolish either, and I am not again Fu Jian — when would I join battle with him?
translations.idiomatic: You always want a pitched battle; I am not so foolish, and I am no Fu Jian — when would I give you one?

sentences.zh: 晝則遣騎圍繞，夜則離彼百里外宿；

translations.literal: By day I send cavalry to surround him; by night I camp a hundred li from him;
translations.idiomatic: By day I ring you with cavalry; by night I camp a hundred li away;

sentences.zh: 吳人正有斫營伎，彼募人以來，不過行五十里，天已明矣。

translations.literal: Wu people indeed have the skill of raiding camps; if he recruits men to come, they can march no more than fifty li before dawn is already bright.
translations.idiomatic: Your Wu raiders are skilled at night attacks — but if you recruit men to strike my camp, they cannot march fifty li before dawn.

sentences.zh: 彼募人之首，豈得不為我有哉！

translations.literal: The heads of men he recruits — how could they not become mine!
translations.idiomatic: Their heads will be mine before they reach me!

sentences.zh: 「彼公時舊臣雖老，猶有智策，知今已殺盡，豈非天資我邪！

translations.literal: " His old ministers from the founding era, though aged, still had strategies; knowing he has now killed them all — is this not Heaven endowing me!
translations.idiomatic: " Your founding ministers, though old, still had wisdom; you have killed them all — has Heaven not blessed me!

sentences.zh: 取彼亦不須我兵刃，此有善咒婆羅門，當使鬼縛以來耳。」

translations.literal: Taking him needs not my blades; here is a Brahmin skilled in spells — I shall have ghosts bind him and bring him."
translations.idiomatic: I need no sword to take you — I have a Brahmin adept at spells who will send ghosts to bind you and bring you to me."

sentences.zh: 侍中、左衛將軍江湛遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Guards General Jiang Zhan was transferred to Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary and Left Guards General Jiang Zhan was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 湛性公廉，與僕射徐湛之並為上所寵信，時稱「江徐」。

translations.literal: Zhan's nature was fair and incorrupt; together with Vice Director Xu Tanzhi he was favored and trusted by the emperor; at the time they were called "Jiang and Xu."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was upright and incorruptible; he and Vice Director Xu Tanzhi were both favorites of the emperor and were known together as "Jiang and Xu."

sentences.zh: 魏司徒崔浩，自恃才略及魏主所寵任，專制朝權，嘗薦冀、定、相、幽、并五州之士數十人，皆起家為郡守。

translations.literal: Wei Minister of Works Cui Hao, relying on his talent and strategy and on the Wei ruler's favor and trust, monopolized court power; he once recommended several tens of men from the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Xiang, You, and Bing, all of whom began their careers as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao, Minister of Works of Wei, took advantage of his ability and of the emperor's favor to dominate the court. On one occasion he recommended several dozen scholars from Ji, Ding, Xiang, You, and Bing, and every one of them was launched straight into a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太守晃曰：「先征之人，亦州郡之選也；

translations.literal: Grand Prefect Huang said: "Those recruited earlier were also selections from the provinces and commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huang said, "The men you recruited before were chosen from the provinces too;

sentences.zh: 在職已久，勤勞未答，宜先補郡縣，以新征者代為郎吏。

translations.literal: they have long held office, their labor unrewarded — it is fitting first to appoint them to counties and districts, and let the newly recruited men replace them as clerks in the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: they have served a long time without proper reward for their work. You ought to give them county and district posts first, and let the new recruits take their places as secretariat clerks.

sentences.zh: 且守令治民，宜得更事者。」

translations.literal: Moreover, for prefects and magistrates who govern the people, it is fitting to have men with more experience."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, prefects and magistrates who govern the people ought to be men with more experience."

sentences.zh: 浩固爭而遣之。

translations.literal: Hao stubbornly contested this and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: Hao argued fiercely against it and sent the men out anyway.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、領著作郎高允聞之，謂東宮博士管恬曰：「崔公其不免乎！

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Gentleman and concurrent Director of Compilation Gao Yun, hearing of this, said to Eastern Palace Erudite Guan Tian: "Master Cui will surely not escape calamity!
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yun, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat and acting Director of Compilation, heard of this, he said to Eastern Palace Erudite Guan Tian, "I fear Master Cui will not escape disaster!

sentences.zh: 苟遂其非而校勝於上，將何以堪之！」

translations.literal: If he indulges his wrongs and contends for victory over his sovereign, how will he be able to bear what follows!"
translations.idiomatic: If he keeps pressing his own way and tries to prevail over the throne, how will he ever survive the reckoning!"

sentences.zh: 魏主以浩監秘書事，使與高允等共撰《國記》，曰：「務從實錄。」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler put Hao in charge of supervising secretariat affairs and had him compile the National Chronicle together with Gao Yun and others, saying: "You must follow the true record."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor put Hao in charge of the secretariat and ordered him to compile the National Chronicle with Gao Yun and others, instructing them, "Write only what truly happened."

sentences.zh: 著作令史閔湛、郗標，性巧佞，為浩所寵信。

translations.literal: Compilation clerks Min Zhan and Xi Biao were by nature clever and sycophantic, and were favored and trusted by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The compilation clerks Min Zhan and Xi Biao were clever flatterers, and Hao favored and trusted them.

sentences.zh: 浩嘗注《易》及《論語》、《詩》、《書》，湛、標上疏言：「馬、鄭、王、賈不如浩之精微，乞收境內諸書，班浩所注，令天下習業。

translations.literal: Hao had once annotated the Book of Changes, the Analects, the Odes, and the Documents; Zhan and Biao submitted a memorial saying: "Ma, Zheng, Wang, and Jia are not as subtle and precise as Hao; we beg that all books within the realm be collected and Hao's annotations distributed, so that the empire may study them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had annotated the Book of Changes, the Analects, the Odes, and the Documents. Zhan and Biao memorialized the throne: "The commentaries of Ma, Zheng, Wang, and Jia cannot match the depth of Hao's work. We ask that books throughout the realm be gathered in, that Hao's notes be issued, and that the whole empire take them as its standard of study.

sentences.zh: 並求敕浩注《禮傳》，令後生得觀正義。」

translations.literal: They also requested an order for Hao to annotate the Ritual Traditions, so that later generations might view the correct meaning."
translations.idiomatic: They also asked that Hao be commanded to annotate the Ritual Traditions, so that future students might learn the true interpretation."

sentences.zh: 浩亦薦湛、標有著述才。

translations.literal: Hao also recommended Zhan and Biao as having talent for writing and compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Hao in turn praised Zhan and Biao as men of literary talent.

sentences.zh: 湛、標又勸浩刊所撰《國史》於石，以彰直筆。

translations.literal: Zhan and Biao further urged Hao to carve the National History he had compiled upon stone, to display the upright brush.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan and Biao then urged Hao to have the National History they had written cut into stone, proclaiming it an act of honest historiography.

sentences.zh: 高允聞之，謂著作郎宗欽曰：「湛、標所營，分寸之間，恐為崔門萬世之禍，吾徒亦無□類矣！」

translations.literal: Gao Yun, hearing of this, said to Compilation Gentleman Zong Qin: "In the smallest measure of what Zhan and Biao are undertaking, I fear it will become a calamity for the Cui house for ten thousand generations — we too will have no one spared!"
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yun heard this, he told Compilation Gentleman Zong Qin, "In the smallest detail of what Zhan and Biao are plotting, I see a disaster for the Cui clan that will last ten thousand generations — we too will not escape ruin!"

sentences.zh: 浩竟用湛、標議，刊石立於郊壇東，方百步，用功三百萬。

translations.literal: Hao in the end adopted the proposal of Zhan and Biao; the stone was carved and erected east of the suburban altar, an area a hundred paces square, costing three million in labor.
translations.idiomatic: Hao took their advice. The history was carved on stone and set up east of the suburban altar on a plot a hundred paces square, at a cost of three million in labor.

sentences.zh: 浩書魏之先世，事皆詳實，列於衢路，往來見者鹹以為言。

translations.literal: What Hao wrote of Wei's forebears was in every case detailed and true, set out along the public roads; all who passed and saw it took it as a topic of talk.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's account of Wei's early rulers was detailed and unsparing, displayed along the public roads where every passerby had something to say about it.

sentences.zh: 北人無不忿恚，相與譖浩於帝，以為暴揚國惡。

translations.literal: Northerners were without exception indignant; together they slandered Hao to the emperor, saying he had violently exposed the state's shame.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners were furious, and one after another they denounced Hao to the emperor, accusing him of publicly airing the dynasty's disgrace.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，使有司案浩及秘書郎吏等罪狀。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered the authorities to investigate the crimes of Hao and the secretariat clerks and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered an inquiry into the offenses of Hao and the secretariat staff.

sentences.zh: 初，遼東公翟黑子有寵於帝，奉使并州，受布千匹。

translations.literal: Initially, Duke of Liaodong Zhai Heizi was favored by the emperor; on a mission to Bing Province he accepted a bribe of a thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhai Heizi, Duke of Liaodong, had been a favorite of the emperor. Sent on a mission to Bing Province, he accepted a bribe of a thousand bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 事覺，黑子謀於高允曰：「主上問我，當以實告，為當諱之？」

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, Heizi consulted Gao Yun, saying: "When the sovereign questions me, ought I to tell the truth, or ought I to conceal it?"
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was discovered, Heizi asked Gao Yun's advice: "If the emperor questions me, should I confess honestly, or should I hide it?"

sentences.zh: 允曰：「公帷幄寵臣，有罪首實，庶或見原，不可重為欺罔也。」

translations.literal: Yun said: "You are a favored minister at the ruler's side; if guilty, to confess first — perhaps you may be forgiven — you must not again practice deception."
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied, "You are a trusted counselor at the emperor's side. If you are guilty and confess first, you may yet be pardoned. You must not deceive him again."

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎崔覽、公孫質曰：「若首實，罪不可測，不如諱之」黑子怨允曰：「君奈何誘人就死地！」

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Gentleman Cui Lan and Gongsun Zhi said: "If you confess first, the punishment cannot be measured — better to conceal it." Heizi resented Yun, saying: "Sir, why do you lure a man toward death!"
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Gentleman Cui Lan and Gongsun Zhi said, "If you confess, the penalty may be beyond reckoning — better to lie." Heizi turned on Yun in anger: "Why are you sending me to my death!"

sentences.zh: 入見帝，不以實對，帝怒，殺之。

translations.literal: He went in to see the emperor and did not answer truthfully; the emperor was enraged and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He went before the emperor and lied. The emperor was furious and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 帝使允授太子經。

translations.literal: The emperor had Yun instruct the crown prince in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Yun to teach the crown prince the classics.

sentences.zh: 及崔浩被收，太子召允至東宮，因留宿。

translations.literal: When Cui Hao was arrested, the crown prince summoned Yun to the Eastern Palace and kept him overnight.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hao was taken into custody, the crown prince summoned Yun to the Eastern Palace and kept him there overnight.

sentences.zh: 明旦，與俱入朝，至宮門，謂允曰：「入見至尊，吾自導卿；

translations.literal: At dawn the next day he entered court together with him; at the palace gate he said to Yun: "When we go in to see the sovereign, I myself will guide you;
translations.idiomatic: The next morning they went to court together. At the palace gate the crown prince said to Yun, "When we enter to see the emperor, I will guide you;

sentences.zh: 脫至尊有問，但依吾語。」

translations.literal: if perchance the sovereign questions you, simply follow my words."
translations.idiomatic: if he questions you, say only what I tell you."

sentences.zh: 允曰：「為何等事也？」

translations.literal: Yun said: "Regarding what sort of matter?"
translations.idiomatic: Yun asked, "What is this about?"

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「人自知之。」

translations.literal: The crown prince said: "Each man knows in himself."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "You know perfectly well."

sentences.zh: 太子見帝言「高允小心真密旦微賤；

translations.literal: The crown prince, seeing the emperor, said: "Gao Yun is careful, truly discreet, and slight and lowly in rank;
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor, the crown prince said, "Gao Yun is cautious and tight-lipped, and holds only a humble, low-ranking post;

sentences.zh: 制由崔浩，請赦其死。」

translations.literal: control lay with Cui Hao — I beg that his death be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao was in charge of everything. I ask that his life be spared."

sentences.zh: 帝召允，問曰：「《國書》皆浩所為乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yun and asked: "Was the National Book entirely the work of Hao?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yun and asked, "Was the National History entirely Hao's work?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「《太祖記》，前著作郎鄧淵所為；

translations.literal: He replied: "The Annals of the Founding Emperor were the work of the former Compilation Gentleman Deng Yuan;
translations.idiomatic: Yun answered, "The Annals of the Founding Emperor were written by the former Compilation Gentleman Deng Yuan;

sentences.zh: 《先帝記》及《今記》，臣與浩共為之。

translations.literal: the Annals of the Late Emperor and the Current Annals — your subject and Hao compiled them together.
translations.idiomatic: the Annals of the Late Emperor and the Current Annals were written jointly by Hao and myself.

sentences.zh: 然浩所領事多，總裁而已；

translations.literal: Yet Hao oversaw many affairs and merely supervised in general;
translations.idiomatic: But Hao had many duties and served mainly as general editor;

sentences.zh: 至於著述，臣多於浩。」

translations.literal: as for the actual writing, your subject did more than Hao."
translations.idiomatic: as for the actual writing, I did more than he did."

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「允罪甚於浩，何以得生！」

translations.literal: The emperor said in anger: "Yun's crime is greater than Hao's — how can he be allowed to live!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, "Yun's guilt is greater than Hao's — why should he live!"

sentences.zh: 太子懼，曰：「天威嚴重，允小臣，迷亂失次耳。

translations.literal: The crown prince, afraid, said: "Heaven's majesty is severe; Yun is a petty official — he was confused and lost order, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, frightened, said, "Your majesty's presence is overwhelming. Yun is only a minor official — he was confused and spoke out of turn.

sentences.zh: 臣向問，皆雲浩所為。」

translations.literal: When your subject questioned him earlier, he all said it was Hao's work."
translations.idiomatic: When I questioned him just now, he said it was all Hao's work."

sentences.zh: 帝問允：「信如東官所言乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Yun: "Is it truly as the Eastern Palace says?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Yun: "Is what the crown prince says true?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣罪當滅族，不敢虛妄。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject's crime merits extermination of the clan — I dare not speak falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Yun answered, "My crime deserves the extinction of my whole clan. I dare not lie.

sentences.zh: 殿下以臣侍講日久，哀臣，欲丐其生耳，實不問臣，臣亦無此言，不敢迷亂。」

translations.literal: Your Highness, because your subject has long served as lecturer, pitied me and wished to beg for my life — in truth he did not question me, and I never said such words; I dare not be confused."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince has known me as his teacher for many years and wished to save my life. He never questioned me, I never said what he claims, and I will not pretend otherwise out of confusion."

sentences.zh: 帝顧謂太子曰：「直哉！

translations.literal: The emperor turned and said to the crown prince: "How upright!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked at the crown prince and said, "What integrity!

sentences.zh: 此人情所難，而允能為之！

translations.literal: This is what human feeling finds hard, yet Yun was able to do it!
translations.idiomatic: That is what most men cannot bring themselves to do — yet Yun did it!

sentences.zh: 臨死不易辭，信也：為臣不欺君，貞也。

translations.literal: Facing death yet not altering his words — that is trustworthiness; as minister not deceiving his ruler — that is constancy.
translations.idiomatic: To hold to one's words even at the point of death is trustworthiness; as a minister, not to deceive one's ruler is constancy.

sentences.zh: 宜特除其罪以旌之。」

translations.literal: It is fitting specially to remit his crime in order to honor him."
translations.idiomatic: His offense should be specially pardoned as a mark of honor."

sentences.zh: 遂赦之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: And he pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 於是召浩前，臨詰之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Hao forward and interrogated him face to face.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Hao brought forward and questioned him in person.

sentences.zh: 浩惶惑不能對。

translations.literal: Hao, panicked and confused, could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, terrified and at a loss, could not answer.

sentences.zh: 允事事申明，皆有條理。

translations.literal: Yun explained each matter clearly, all with order and reason.
translations.idiomatic: Yun explained every point clearly and in good order.

sentences.zh: 帝命允為詔，誅浩及僚屬宗欽、段承根等，下至僮吏，凡百二十八人，皆夷五族；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yun to draft an edict executing Hao and his subordinates Zong Qin, Duan Chenggen, and others, down to servant clerks — altogether one hundred twenty-eight persons — all with extermination of five clans;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yun to draft an edict condemning Hao and his colleagues Zong Qin, Duan Chenggen, and others, down to the humblest clerks — one hundred twenty-eight men in all — each with the extermination of five generations of kin;

sentences.zh: 允持疑不為。

translations.literal: Yun hesitated and would not do it.
translations.idiomatic: Yun hesitated and refused.

sentences.zh: 帝頻使催切，允乞更一見，然後為詔。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent urgent orders; Yun begged to see him once more, and then he would draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent repeated urgent commands. Yun asked to see him once more before he would write the edict.

sentences.zh: 帝引使前，允曰：「浩之所坐，若更有餘釁，非臣敢知；

translations.literal: The emperor had him brought forward; Yun said: "The offense for which Hao sits — if there are further crimes beyond this, your subject dare not know of them;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him brought forward. Yun said, "If Hao is guilty of other crimes besides this, I cannot say;

sentences.zh: 若直以觸犯，罪不至死。」

translations.literal: if it is solely on account of giving offense, the crime does not reach death."
translations.idiomatic: but if the charge is merely giving offense, the penalty should not be death."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命武士執允。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and ordered warriors to seize Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered guards to seize Yun.

sentences.zh: 太子為之拜請，帝意解，乃曰：「無斯人，當更有數千口死矣。」

translations.literal: The crown prince bowed and pleaded on his behalf; the emperor's mood eased, and he then said: "Without this man, several thousand more lives would have died."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince bowed and pleaded for him. The emperor relented and said, "Without this man, several thousand more people would have died."

sentences.zh: 六月，己亥，詔誅清河崔氏與浩同宗者無遠近，及浩姻家范陽盧氏、太原郭氏、河東柳氏，並夷其族，餘皆止誅其身。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on the day jihai, an edict ordered the execution of the Qinghe Cui clan, all of the same lineage as Hao without regard to nearness or distance, and Hao's affinal families — the Fanyang Lu, the Taiyuan Guo, and the Hedong Liu — all with extermination of their clans; the rest were punished only with execution of the person himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day jihai, an edict condemned to death every member of the Qinghe Cui clan related to Hao, near or distant, together with his in-laws among the Fanyang Lu, the Taiyuan Guo, and the Hedong Liu — all their clans were exterminated. The rest were executed only in their own persons.

sentences.zh: 執浩置檻內，送城南，衛士數十人溲其上，呼聲嗷嗷，聞於行路。

translations.literal: Hao was seized, placed in a cage, and sent to the south of the city; several tens of guards urinated upon him; his cries of anguish were heard along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was seized, put in a cage, and sent south of the city. Dozens of guards urinated on him. His wailing could be heard from the road.

sentences.zh: 宗欽臨刑歎曰：「高允其殆聖乎！」

translations.literal: Zong Qin, facing execution, sighed and said: "Gao Yun is perhaps nearly a sage!"
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of execution Zong Qin sighed and said, "Gao Yun is almost a sage!"

sentences.zh: 它日，太子讓允曰：「人亦當知機。

translations.literal: Another day the crown prince reproached Yun, saying: "A man ought also to know the moment.
translations.idiomatic: On another day the crown prince reproached Yun: "A man should know when to bend.

sentences.zh: 吾欲為卿脫死，既聞端緒，而卿終不從，激怒帝如此。

translations.literal: I wished to save you from death; you had already heard how the matter began, yet in the end you would not follow — and so you provoked the emperor to such anger.
translations.idiomatic: I was trying to save your life. You heard how I meant to help, yet you refused to go along — and you provoked the emperor's wrath like that.

sentences.zh: 每念之，使人心悸。」

translations.literal: Whenever I think of it, it makes the heart tremble."
translations.idiomatic: Even now, when I think of it, my heart still quakes."

sentences.zh: 允曰：「夫史者，所以記人主善惡，為將來勸戒，故人主有所畏忌，慎其舉措。

translations.literal: Yun said: "Historians exist to record the good and evil of rulers, to provide admonition for the future; therefore rulers have things they fear and respect, and are careful in their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied, "Historians record a ruler's good and evil deeds so that future ages may take warning. That is why rulers feel restraint and watch what they do.

sentences.zh: 崔浩孤負聖恩，以私慾沒其廉潔，愛憎蔽其公直，此浩之責也。

translations.literal: Cui Hao betrayed sacred favor, letting private desire drown his integrity, letting love and hate blind his public uprightness — that is Hao's responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao betrayed the emperor's trust, letting private desire corrupt his integrity and personal feeling cloud his judgment — that is Hao's fault alone.

sentences.zh: 至於書朝廷起居，言國家得失，此為史之大體，未為多違。

translations.literal: As for writing the court's daily affairs and speaking of the state's gains and losses — that is the great substance of history, and was not greatly transgressive.
translations.idiomatic: But to record the court's daily business and speak plainly of the state's successes and failures — that is the historian's proper duty, and it was no great crime.

sentences.zh: 臣與浩實同其事，死生榮辱，義無獨殊。

translations.literal: Your subject and Hao truly shared the same task; in life and death, honor and disgrace, by right there could be no separate exception.
