translations.idiomatic: Hao and I did the same work. In life or death, honor or shame, I had no right to stand apart.

sentences.zh: 誠荷殿下再造之慈，違心苟免，非臣所願也。」

translations.literal: Truly I am indebted to Your Highness's grace in giving me new life, but to violate my heart and seek escape by pretense — that is not what your subject wishes."
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply grateful that you tried to give me a second life, but to save myself by going against my conscience is not what I wanted."

sentences.zh: 太子動容稱歎。

translations.literal: The crown prince was moved and praised him in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was deeply moved and praised him.

sentences.zh: 允退，謂人曰：「我不奉東宮指導者，恐負翟黑子故也。」

translations.literal: When Yun withdrew, he said to others: "The reason I did not follow the Eastern Palace's guidance was that I feared to fail Zhai Heizi."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Yun told others, "The reason I would not follow the crown prince's instructions was that I did not want to fail Zhai Heizi."

sentences.zh: 初，冀州刺史崔賾，武城男崔模，與浩同宗而別族；

translations.literal: Initially, Ji Province Inspector Cui Ze and Baron of Wucheng Cui Mo were of the same clan as Hao but a separate branch;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Ze, inspector of Ji Province, and Cui Mo, Baron of Wucheng, belonged to a collateral branch of Hao's clan;

sentences.zh: 浩常輕侮之，由是不睦。

translations.literal: Hao often treated them with contempt, and for this reason they were not on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had often treated them with contempt, and relations between them were bad.

sentences.zh: 及浩誅，二家獨得免。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed, these two families alone were spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was condemned, those two families alone were spared.

sentences.zh: 賾，逞之子也。

translations.literal: Ze was the son of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was the son of Cui Cheng.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，魏主北巡陰山。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, the Wei ruler toured the north to Mount Yin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou the Wei emperor made a northern tour to Mount Yin.

sentences.zh: 魏主既誅崔浩而悔之，會北部尚書宣城公李孝伯病篤，或傳已卒，魏主悼之曰：「李宣城可惜！」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler, having executed Cui Hao, regretted it; it happened that Northern Department Minister Duke of Xuancheng Li Xiaobo was gravely ill, and some reported he had already died; the Wei ruler mourned him, saying: "Li of Xuancheng — how regrettable!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor already regretted having executed Cui Hao. Just then Northern Department Minister Li Xiaobo, Duke of Xuancheng, fell gravely ill, and word spread that he had died. The emperor grieved and said, "Li of Xuancheng — what a loss!"

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「朕失言，崔司徒可惜，李宣城可哀！」

translations.literal: Then he said: "I spoke wrongly — Minister of Works Cui is regrettable; Li of Xuancheng is pitiable!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he corrected himself: "I misspoke. Minister Cui is the one to mourn; Li of Xuancheng is merely to be pitied."

sentences.zh: 孝伯，順之從父弟也，自浩之誅，軍國謀議皆出孝伯，寵眷亞於浩。

translations.literal: Xiaobo was the younger paternal cousin of Shunzhi; since Hao's execution, military and state counsel all came from Xiaobo, and favor fell only slightly short of Hao's.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo was a cousin of Li Shunzhi. After Hao's death, military and state policy passed largely into his hands, and the emperor's favor for him was second only to what Hao had enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 初，車師大帥車伊洛世服於魏，魏拜伊洛平西將軍，封前部王。

translations.literal: Initially, the great chieftain of Cheshi, Che Yiluo, had for generations submitted to Wei; Wei appointed Yiluo General Who Pacifies the West and enfeoffed him as King of the Front Division.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yiluo, the great chieftain of Cheshi, had long submitted to Wei. The court made him General Who Pacifies the West and enfeoffed him as King of the Front Division.

sentences.zh: 伊洛將入朝，沮渠無諱斷其路，伊洛屢與無諱戰，破之。

translations.literal: When Yiluo was about to enter court, Juqu Wuhui cut off his route; Yiluo repeatedly fought Wuhui and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: As Yiluo was on his way to court, Juqu Wuhui blocked his path. Yiluo fought him again and again and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 無諱卒，弟安周奪其子乾壽兵，伊洛遣人說乾壽，乾壽遂帥其民五百餘家奔魏；

translations.literal: Wuhui died; his younger brother Anzhou seized the troops of his son Ganshou; Yiluo sent men to persuade Ganshou, and Ganshou thereupon led more than five hundred households of his people to flee to Wei;
translations.idiomatic: When Wuhui died, his brother Anzhou seized the army of Wuhui's son Ganshou. Yiluo sent envoys to win Ganshou over, and Ganshou led more than five hundred households into Wei territory;

sentences.zh: 伊洛又說李寶弟欽等五十餘人下之，皆送於魏。

translations.literal: Yiluo also persuaded Li Bao's younger brother Qin and more than fifty others to submit; all were sent to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yiluo also persuaded Li Bao's brother Qin and more than fifty others to surrender, and they were all sent on to Wei.

sentences.zh: 伊洛西擊焉耆，留其子歇守城。

translations.literal: Yiluo struck west against Yanqi, leaving his son Xie to guard the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yiluo marched west against Yanqi and left his son Xie to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 沮渠安周引柔然兵間道襲之，攻拔其城。

translations.literal: Juqu Anzhou led Rouran troops by a hidden route to strike him, attacked, and captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Anzhou brought Rouran troops by a hidden route, struck suddenly, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 歇走就伊洛，共收餘眾，保焉耆鎮，遣使上書於魏主，言：「為沮渠氏所攻，首尾八年，百姓饑窮，無以自存。

translations.literal: Xie fled to join Yiluo; together they gathered the remaining forces and held Yanqi garrison; they sent envoys with a memorial to the Wei ruler, saying: "We have been attacked by the Juqu clan for eight years from beginning to end; the people are hungry and destitute and have no means to survive.
translations.idiomatic: Xie fled to his father. Together they rallied the survivors and held the garrison at Yanqi. They sent a memorial to the Wei emperor saying, "We have been under attack by the Juqu for eight years. Our people are starving and have no way to live.

sentences.zh: 臣今棄國出奔，得免者才三分之一，已至焉耆東境，乞垂賑救！」

translations.literal: Your subject now abandons the state and flees; those who escape amount to only one third; we have already reached the eastern border of Yanqi — we beg your grace to grant relief and rescue!"
translations.idiomatic: We have abandoned our country and fled. Barely a third of our people escaped. We have reached the eastern border of Yanqi and beg for aid!"

sentences.zh: 魏主詔開焉耆倉以賑之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered the Yanqi granaries opened to give them relief.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor ordered the Yanqi granaries opened for their relief.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王慕利延為魏所逼，上表求入保越巂，上許之；

translations.literal: Tuyuhun King Murong Muliyan, pressed by Wei, submitted a memorial requesting to enter and take refuge in Yuexi; the emperor granted it;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Muliyan, king of Tuyuhun, hard pressed by Wei, memorialized asking to take refuge in Yuexi, and the Song emperor agreed;

sentences.zh: 慕利延竟不至。

translations.literal: Muliyan in the end did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Muliyan never came.

sentences.zh: 上欲伐魏，丹楊尹徐湛之、吏部尚書江湛、彭城太守王玄謨等並勸之；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to attack Wei; Danyang Prefect Xu Tanzhi, Minister of the Masters of Writing Jiang Zhan, Pengcheng Prefect Wang Xuanmo, and others all urged it;
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor wanted to attack Wei. Xu Tanzhi, prefect of Danyang; Jiang Zhan, Minister of Personnel; Wang Xuanmo, prefect of Pengcheng; and others all urged him on;

sentences.zh: 左軍將軍劉康祖以為「歲月已晚，請待明年。」

translations.literal: Left Army General Liu Kangzu held that "the months are already late — I request waiting until next year."
translations.idiomatic: Left Army General Liu Kangzu argued, "The season is already late. Wait until next year."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「北方苦虜虐政，義徒並起。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The north suffers under the barbarians' cruel government; men of righteousness rise together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The north groans under Wei oppression. Righteous men are rising everywhere.

sentences.zh: 頓兵一週，沮向義之心，不可。」

translations.literal: To halt the army even one cycle would dampen the hearts of those turning toward righteousness — that cannot be."
translations.idiomatic: To delay the army even one season would crush their hope of deliverance. That we cannot do."

sentences.zh: 太子步兵校尉沈慶之諫曰：「我步彼騎，其勢不敵。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Footsoldier Commandant Shen Qingzhi remonstrated, saying: "We on foot, they on horse — the momentum cannot match.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi, Crown Prince Footsoldier Commandant, warned, "Our infantry against their cavalry — the odds are against us.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟再行無功，到彥之失利而返。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji on a second campaign achieved nothing; Dao Yanzhi suffered defeat and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji's second northern campaign came to nothing, and Dao Yanzhi was beaten and driven back.

sentences.zh: 今料王玄謨等，未逾兩將，六軍之盛，不過往時，恐重辱王師。」

translations.literal: Now judging Wang Xuanmo and the rest, they do not surpass the two earlier generals; the grandeur of the Six Armies does not exceed times past — I fear the imperial army will again suffer disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: Judging by men like Wang Xuanmo, we have no better commanders than before, and the host we can field is no stronger than in those earlier campaigns. I fear the imperial forces will be humiliated again."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「王師再屈，別自有由，道濟美寇自資，彥之中塗疾動。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The imperial army was twice defeated, each time for its own reasons — Daoji enriched the enemy to his own profit; Yanzhi was stricken with illness mid-route.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Our armies were beaten twice, but for different reasons — Tan Daoji fattened the enemy for his own gain, and Dao Yanzhi fell ill on the march.

sentences.zh: 虜所恃者唯馬；

translations.literal: What the barbarians rely on is horses alone;
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians depend on one thing only — their horses;

sentences.zh: 今夏水浩汗，河道流通，泛舟北下，碻磝必走，滑台小戍，易可覆拔。

translations.literal: This summer the waters are vast and surging, the river channels flow freely; sailing boats northward, Qiaoao will surely flee, and the small garrison at Huatai can easily be overrun and taken.
translations.idiomatic: This summer the rivers run high and free. If we put boats on the water and sail north, the enemy at Qiaoao will flee, and the small garrison at Huatai will fall easily.

sentences.zh: 克此二城，館谷弔民，虎牢、洛陽，自然不固。

translations.literal: Taking these two cities, storing grain and comforting the people, Hulao and Luoyang will naturally not hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Seize those two cities, stock them with grain, and win over the people — Hulao and Luoyang will not long stand.

sentences.zh: 比及冬初，城守相接，虜馬過河，即成擒也。」

translations.literal: By the beginning of winter, city defenders will connect in a line; when the barbarian horses cross the river, they will be captured at once."
translations.idiomatic: By early winter our garrisons will form an unbroken line. When their cavalry tries to ford the rivers, we will take them all."

sentences.zh: 慶之又固陳不可。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi again firmly stated that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi persisted in objecting that the plan was unwise.

sentences.zh: 上使徐港之、江湛難之。

translations.literal: The emperor had Xu Tanzhi and Jiang Zhan argue against him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xu Tanzhi and Jiang Zhan to rebut him.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「治國譬如治家，耕當問奴，織當訪婢。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi said: "Governing a state is like managing a household — when plowing one should ask the slave, when weaving one should consult the maid.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi said, "Governing a country is like running a household. Ask the farmhand about plowing and the maid about weaving.

sentences.zh: 陛下今欲伐國，而與白面書生輩謀之，事何由濟！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty now wishes to attack a state, yet plans with pale-faced scholar types — how can the affair succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty means to make war, but you take counsel from pale-faced bookmen — how can that ever succeed?"

sentences.zh: 上大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 太子劭及護軍將軍蕭思話亦諫，上皆不從。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Shao and Protector of the Army General Xiao Sihua also remonstrated; the emperor would not heed any of them.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Shao and Protector of the Army Xiao Sihua offered warnings as well, but the emperor refused them all.

sentences.zh: 魏主聞上將北伐，復與上書曰：「彼此和好日久，而彼志無厭，誘我邊民。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler, hearing that the emperor would launch a northern campaign, again wrote to him, saying: "We have been at peace for a long time, yet your side's ambition knows no limit, seducing my frontier people.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor learned the Song ruler meant to march north, he wrote again: "We have lived in peace for years, yet your appetite is never sated, and you lure away my border people.

sentences.zh: 今春南巡，聊省我民，驅之使還。

translations.literal: This spring I toured south only to look in on my people and drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: My southern tour this spring was merely to check on my subjects and send them home.

sentences.zh: 今聞彼欲自來，設能至中山及桑干川，隨意而行，來亦不迎，去亦不送。

translations.literal: Now I hear you wish to come in person — if you can reach Zhongshan and the Sanggan River, go as you please; coming I shall not welcome, going I shall not escort.
translations.idiomatic: I hear you plan to come yourself. If you can reach Zhongshan and the Sanggan, travel as you like — I will neither welcome you nor see you off.

sentences.zh: 若厭其區宇者，可來平城居，我亦往揚州，相與易。

translations.literal: If you tire of your territory, you may come live at Pingcheng while I go to Yangzhou — we can swap.
translations.idiomatic: If you have grown tired of your own domain, come take Pingcheng and I will move to Yangzhou — we can trade capitals.

sentences.zh: 彼年已五十，未嘗出戶，雖自力而來，如三歲嬰兒，與我鮮卑生長馬上者果如何哉！

translations.literal: You are already fifty and have never left your door; even if you force yourself to come, you will be like a three-year-old infant — what can you truly do against us Xianbei who grew up on horseback!
translations.idiomatic: You are fifty years old and have never left your palace. Even if you drag yourself here, you will be no more than a toddling child — what match are you for us Xianbei, reared in the saddle?

sentences.zh: 更無餘物可以相與，今送獵馬十二匹並氈、藥等物。

translations.literal: I have nothing else to offer you — I now send twelve hunting horses together with felt, medicines, and such items.
translations.idiomatic: I have nothing else to give you, so I send twelve hunting horses, along with felt, medicines, and the like.

sentences.zh: 彼來道遠，馬力不足，可乘；

translations.literal: Your road here is long and your horses' strength insufficient — these you may ride;
translations.idiomatic: The journey is long and your horses will fail — use these instead;

sentences.zh: 或不服水土，藥可自療也。」

translations.literal: Or if you cannot tolerate the water and soil, the medicine can treat yourself."
translations.idiomatic: If the climate disagrees with you, the medicine should set you right."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚午，詔曰：「虜近雖摧挫，獸心靡革。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on gengwu day, an edict said: "The barbarians, though recently beaten back, their beastly hearts have not changed.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day gengwu, an edict proclaimed: "The enemy was checked not long ago, yet his savage heart is unchanged.

sentences.zh: 比得河朔、秦、雍華戎表疏，歸訴困棘，跂望綏拯，潛相糾結以候王師；

translations.literal: Recently we have received memorials from Chinese and barbarians of Heshuo, Qin, and Yong, each returning to lodge complaints of distress, standing on tiptoe to look for relief and salvation, secretly joining together to await the imperial army;
translations.idiomatic: Memorials have lately reached us from Chinese and tribesmen across Heshuo, Qin, and Yong, each pleading their hardship and straining toward deliverance, secretly rallying to await the imperial army;

sentences.zh: 芮芮亦遣間使遠輸誠款，誓為掎角；

translations.literal: Rouran too has sent secret envoys from afar bearing sincere pledges, swearing to act in pincer support;
translations.idiomatic: Rouran too has sent secret envoys from afar with pledges of loyalty, vowing to strike in concert with us;

sentences.zh: 經略之會，實在茲日。

translations.literal: The moment for strategic expansion is truly this day.
translations.idiomatic: The hour for grand strategy is now.

sentences.zh: 可遣寧朔將軍王玄謨帥太子步兵校尉沈慶之、鎮軍咨議參軍申坦水軍入河，受督於青、冀二州刺史蕭斌；

translations.literal: Pacifying the North General Wang Xuanmo may be sent leading Crown Prince Footsoldier Commandant Shen Qingzhi and Pacifying Army Consultant Staff Officer Shen Tan with the river fleet into the Yellow River, under the command of the Governors of Qing and Ji, Xiao Bin;
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying the North General Wang Xuanmo shall lead Crown Prince Footsoldier Commandant Shen Qingzhi and Pacifying Army staff officer Shen Tan with the river fleet into the Yellow River, under Qing and Ji prefect Xiao Bin;

sentences.zh: 太子左衛率臧質、驍騎將軍王方回徑造許、洛；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Left Guard Leader Zang Zhi and Valiant Cavalry General Wang Fanghui shall press directly toward Xu and Luo;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Left Guard Leader Zang Zhi and Valiant Cavalry General Wang Fanghui shall march straight on Xuchang and Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 徐、兗二州刺史武陵王駿、豫州刺史南平王鑠各勒所部，東西齊舉；

translations.literal: The Governors of Xu and Yan, Prince of Wuling Jun, and Governor of Yu, Prince of Nanping Shuo, shall each lead their forces, rising together east and west;
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Yan prefect Wuling Wang Jun and Yu prefect Nanping Wang Shuo shall each mobilize their commands, advancing together from east and west;

sentences.zh: 梁、南、北秦三州刺史劉秀之震盪汧、隴；

translations.literal: The Governors of Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, Liu Xiuzhi, shall shake Qian and Long;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuzhi, prefect of Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, shall strike Qian and Long;

sentences.zh: 太尉江夏王義恭出次彭城，為眾軍節度。」

translations.literal: Grand Commander Prince of Jiangxia Yigong shall go out and encamp at Pengcheng, directing all the armies."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander Jiangxia Wang Yigong shall establish headquarters at Pengcheng and coordinate all forces.

sentences.zh: 坦，鐘之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Tan was the great-grandson of Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tan was the great-grandson of Shen Zhong.

sentences.zh: 是時軍旅大起，王公、妃主及朝士、牧守，下至富民，各獻金帛、雜物以助國用。

translations.literal: At this time armies were raised on a great scale; princes, princesses, court officials, and regional governors, down to wealthy commoners, each contributed gold, silk, and miscellaneous goods to aid state expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Armies were mustered on a vast scale. Princes, princesses, courtiers, and prefects — even wealthy commoners — sent gold, silk, and goods to support the war chest.

sentences.zh: 又以兵力不足，悉發青、冀、徐、豫、二兗六州三五民丁，倩使暫行，符到十日裝束；

translations.literal: Because troops were insufficient, all common men in their prime from the six provinces Qing, Ji, Xu, Yu, and the two Yan were conscripted, hired for temporary service; when the order arrived they had ten days to prepare;
translations.idiomatic: Forces still fell short, so every able-bodied man in Qing, Ji, Xu, Yu, and the two Yan provinces was drafted for temporary service — ten days to assemble once the order arrived;

sentences.zh: 緣江五郡集廣陵，緣淮三郡集盱眙。

translations.literal: Five commanderies along the Yangzi gathered at Guangling; three commanderies along the Huai gathered at Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Five Yangzi commanderies mustered at Guangling; three Huai commanderies at Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 又募中外有馬步眾藝武力之士應科者，皆加厚賞。

translations.literal: They also recruited men inside and outside the court skilled in mounted and foot fighting and martial arts who met the standards, all receiving enriched rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled horsemen and foot soldiers who answered the call, inside and outside the court, were promised lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 有司又奏軍用不充，揚、南徐、兗、江四州富民家貲滿五十萬，僧尼滿二十萬，並四分借一，事息即還。

translations.literal: The offices again reported that military supplies were insufficient; in Yang, Southern Xu, Yan, and Jiang — four provinces — wealthy households with assets of five hundred thousand, and monks and nuns with two hundred thousand, all had one quarter lent by force; when the affair ended it would be returned.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported that war funds still fell short. In Yang, Southern Xu, Yan, and Jiang, wealthy families worth five hundred thousand coins and monasteries worth two hundred thousand were each forced to lend one quarter of their assets — to be repaid when the campaign ended.

sentences.zh: 建武司馬申元吉引兵趨碻磝。

translations.literal: Establishing Martialness Army Major Shen Yuanji led troops toward Qiaoao.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing Martialness army major Shen Yuanji marched on Qiaoao.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，魏濟州刺史王買德棄城走。

translations.literal: On yihai day, Wei Jizhou Governor Wang Maide abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, Wang Maide, Wei governor of Jizhou, abandoned his city and fled.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌遣將軍崔猛攻樂安，魏青州刺史張淮之亦棄城走。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin sent General Cui Meng to attack Le'an; Wei Qingzhou Governor Zhang Huaizhi also abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin sent General Cui Meng against Le'an; Zhang Huaizhi, Wei governor of Qingzhou, fled as well.

sentences.zh: 斌與沈慶之留守碻磝，使王玄謨進圍滑台。

translations.literal: Bin and Shen Qingzhi remained to hold Qiaoao, sending Wang Xuanmo forward to invest Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and Shen Qingzhi stayed to hold Qiaoao while Wang Xuanmo advanced to besiege Huatai.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史隨王誕遣中兵參軍柳元景、振威將軍尹顯祖、奮武將軍曾方平、建武將軍薛安都、略陽太守龐法起將兵出弘農。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Governor Prince of Sui Dan dispatched Central Troops Staff Officer Liu Yuanjing, Shaking Might General Yin Xianzu, Exerting Martialness General Zeng Fangping, Establishing Martialness General Xue Andu, and Lueyang Prefect Pang Faqi to lead troops out from Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Wang Dan, prefect of Yongzhou, sent staff officer Liu Yuanjing, Shaking Might General Yin Xianzu, Exerting Martialness General Zeng Fangping, Establishing Martialness General Xue Andu, and Lueyang prefect Pang Faqi out of Hongnong with their troops.

sentences.zh: 後軍外兵參軍龐季明，年七十餘，自以關中豪右，請入長安招會夷、夏，誕許之；

translations.literal: Rear Army External Troops Staff Officer Pang Jiming, over seventy years old, considering himself a powerful magnate of Guanzhong, requested to enter Chang'an to rally barbarians and Chinese; Dan permitted it;
translations.idiomatic: Pang Jiming, a Rear Army external staff officer in his seventies, claimed standing among the Guanzhong gentry and asked permission to enter Chang'an and rally Chinese and barbarians alike. Dan agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃自貲谷入盧氏，盧氏民趙難納之。

translations.literal: He then entered Lushi from Zigu; the Lushi commoner Zhao Nan received him.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Lushi through Zigu Valley, where a local man named Zhao Nan sheltered him.

sentences.zh: 季明遂誘說士民，應之者甚眾，安都等因之，自熊耳山出；

translations.literal: Jiming then enticed and persuaded gentry and commoners; very many responded, and Andu and the rest, taking advantage of this, emerged from Xiong'er Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: Jiming won over the local people in great numbers. Andu and the others used that opening to break out through Xiong'er Mountain.

sentences.zh: 元景引兵繼進。

translations.literal: Yuanjing led troops in continued advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing followed with the main force.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史南平王鑠遣中兵參軍胡盛之出汝南，梁坦出上蔡向長社。

translations.literal: Yu Governor Prince of Nanping Shuo sent Central Troops Staff Officer Hu Shengshi out from Runan; Liang Tan out from Shangcai toward Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Nanping Wang Shuo, prefect of Yu, sent staff officer Hu Shengshi from Runan and Liang Tan from Shangcai toward Changshe.

sentences.zh: 魏荊州刺史魯爽鎮長社，棄城走。

translations.literal: Wei Jingzhou Governor Lu Shuang defended Changshe and abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang, Wei governor of Jingzhou, held Changshe but abandoned it and fled.

sentences.zh: 爽，軌之子也。

translations.literal: Shuang was the son of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang was the son of Lu Gui.

sentences.zh: 幢主王陽兒擊魏豫州刺史僕蘭，破之，僕蘭奔虎牢；

translations.literal: Pennant Commander Wang Yang'er struck Wei Yuzhou Governor Pulans, defeated him, and Pulans fled to Hulao;
translations.idiomatic: Pennant commander Wang Yang'er routed Pulans, Wei governor of Yuzhou, who fled to Hulao;

sentences.zh: 鑠又遣安蠻司馬劉康祖將兵助坦，進逼虎牢。

translations.literal: Shuo also sent Pacify the Barbarians Army Major Liu Kangzu to lead troops to aid Tan, pressing on Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo sent Pacify the Barbarians major Liu Kangzu to reinforce Tan and press Hulao.

sentences.zh: 魏群臣初聞有宋師，言於魏主，請遣兵救緣河谷帛。

translations.literal: When Wei ministers first heard there were Song armies, they spoke to the Wei ruler, requesting troops be sent to rescue the border garrisons along the river valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei's ministers first heard Song armies were in the field, they urged the Wei emperor to send relief to the river-valley border posts.

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「馬今未肥，天時尚熱，速出必無功。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler said: "The horses are not yet fat, the season is still hot — a swift sortie will surely achieve nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor replied, "Our horses are still lean and the weather still hot. A hasty march will come to nothing.

sentences.zh: 若兵來不止，且還陰山避之。

translations.literal: If the enemy armies keep coming without end, for the time being return to Yin Mountain and avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: If they keep coming, withdraw to Yinshan and let them pass.

sentences.zh: 國人本著羊皮褲，何用綿帛！

translations.literal: Our people by nature wear sheepskin trousers — what need is there for cotton and silk!
translations.idiomatic: Our people wear sheepskin britches by custom — what do we need with cotton and silk?

sentences.zh: 展至十月，吾無憂矣。」

translations.literal: Stretch affairs to the tenth month, and I have no worries."
translations.idiomatic: By October I will have nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 九月，辛卯，魏主引兵南救滑台，命太子晃屯漠南以備柔然，吳王余守平城。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on xinmao day, the Wei ruler led troops south to relieve Huatai, ordering Crown Prince Huang to encamp south of the desert against Rouran, and Prince of Wu Yu to hold Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day xinmao, the Wei emperor marched south to relieve Huatai, leaving Crown Prince Huang south of the desert to guard against Rouran and Prince of Wu Yu to hold Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 庚子，魏發州郡兵五萬分給諸軍。

translations.literal: On gengzi day, Wei mobilized fifty thousand troops from provinces and commanderies, distributing them to the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengzi, Wei mobilized fifty thousand troops from the provinces and distributed them among the armies.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨士眾甚盛，器械精嚴；

translations.literal: Wang Xuanmo's troops and people were very numerous, his weapons and equipment refined and strict;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmo's army was huge and his equipment first-rate;

sentences.zh: 而玄謨貪愎好殺。

translations.literal: Yet Xuanmo was greedy, obstinate, and fond of killing.
translations.idiomatic: But he was greedy, stubborn, and bloodthirsty.

sentences.zh: 初圍滑台，城中多茅屋，眾請以火箭燒之。

translations.literal: When first investing Huatai, the city had many thatched houses; the troops requested fire arrows to burn them.
translations.idiomatic: At the first siege of Huatai, the city was full of thatched roofs. His men asked to burn them with fire arrows.

sentences.zh: 玄謨曰：「彼吾財也，何遽燒之！」

translations.literal: Xuanmo said: "Those are my assets — why burn them so hastily!"
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo said, "That is my property — why burn it so quickly!"

sentences.zh: 城中即撤屋穴處。

translations.literal: The city at once pulled down the houses and dug dwellings into the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders immediately tore down the houses and dug underground shelters.

sentences.zh: 時河、洛之民競出租谷、操兵來赴者日以千數，玄謨不即其長帥而以配私暱；

translations.literal: At that time people of the He and Luo regions vied to offer rent-grain and take up arms to come join — daily numbering in the thousands; Xuanmo did not employ their local leaders but assigned them to his private favorites;
translations.idiomatic: Thousands from the Yellow River and Luoyang region came daily with grain and arms to join him. Xuanmo ignored their local leaders and attached them to his own favorites instead;

sentences.zh: 家付匹布，責大梨八百；

translations.literal: Each household was given one bolt of cloth and charged eight hundred large pears;
translations.idiomatic: Each household received one bolt of cloth — and was charged eight hundred large pears;

sentences.zh: 由是眾心失望。

translations.literal: From this the hearts of the multitude lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: The people's hopes collapsed.

sentences.zh: 攻城數月不下，聞魏救將至，眾請發車為營，玄謨不從。

translations.literal: After months the city was not taken; hearing Wei relief was about to arrive, the troops requested deploying carts to form encampments — Xuanmo would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Months passed without taking the city. When word came that Wei relief was near, his men asked to fortify the camp with wagons. Xuanmo refused.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸亥，魏主至枋頭，使關內侯代人陸真夜與數人犯圍，潛入滑台，撫慰城中，且登城視玄謨營曲折還報。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on guihai day, the Wei ruler reached Fangtou; he sent Within-the-Passes Marquis, a native of Dai, Lu Zhen, who in the night with several men broke through the encirclement, secretly entered Huatai, consoled the city, and moreover climbed the wall to observe the twists of Xuanmo's camp before returning to report.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day guihai, the Wei emperor reached Fangtou. He sent Within-the-Passes marquis Lu Zhen, a man of Dai, who stole through the lines at night with a few companions, entered Huatai in secret, heartened the garrison, climbed the wall to study the layout of Xuanmo's camp, and returned with his report.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏主渡河，眾號百萬，鞞鼓之聲，震動天地；

translations.literal: On yichou day, the Wei ruler crossed the river; the host was proclaimed at a million, the sound of war drums shaking heaven and earth;
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou the Wei emperor crossed the river at the head of an army said to number a million. War drums shook heaven and earth;

sentences.zh: 玄謨懼，退走。

translations.literal: Xuanmo was afraid and retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo panicked and fled.

sentences.zh: 魏人追擊之，死者萬餘人，麾下散亡略盡，委棄軍資器械山積。

translations.literal: The Wei people pursued and struck them; dead numbered over ten thousand, those under his command scattered and fled nearly completely, abandoning military stores and equipment piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Wei cavalry ran them down. More than ten thousand were killed, Xuanmo's force dissolved, and abandoned supplies and weapons piled like hills.

sentences.zh: 先是，玄謨遣鐘離太守垣護下以百舸為前鋒，據石濟，在滑台西南百二十里。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xuanmo had sent Zhongli Prefect Yuan Huzhi downstream with a hundred warships as vanguard, occupying Shiji, one hundred twenty li southwest of Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xuanmo had sent Zhongli prefect Yuan Huzhi downstream with a hundred ships as vanguard, holding Shiji, one hundred twenty li southwest of Huatai.

sentences.zh: 護之聞魏兵將至，馳書勸玄謨急攻曰：「昔武皇攻廣固，死沒者甚眾。

translations.literal: Huzhi, hearing Wei troops were about to arrive, sent a fast letter urging Xuanmo to attack urgently, saying: "Formerly Emperor Wu attacked Guanggu, and those who died were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Wei was on the march, Huzhi wrote urgently urging an all-out assault: "When Emperor Wu stormed Guanggu, the dead were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 況今事迫於曩日，豈得計士眾傷疲！

translations.literal: Moreover today's affair is more pressing than that day — how can one calculate the troops' wounds and fatigue!
translations.idiomatic: Today's crisis is worse — how can you weigh casualties against speed!

sentences.zh: 願以屠城為急。」

translations.literal: I wish you would make slaughtering the city the urgent task."
translations.idiomatic: Take the city at any cost."

sentences.zh: 玄謨不從。

translations.literal: Xuanmo would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及玄謨敗退，不暇報護之。

translations.literal: When Xuanmo was defeated and retreated, he had no time to inform Huzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanmo broke and ran, he had no time to warn Huzhi.

sentences.zh: 魏人以所得玄謨戰艦，連以鐵鎖三重，斷河以絕護之還路。

translations.literal: The Wei people took Xuanmo's warships they had captured, linked them with iron chains in triple layers, and blocked the river to cut off Huzhi's return route.
translations.idiomatic: Wei used Xuanmo's captured warships, chained them in triple lines across the river, and cut off Huzhi's escape.

sentences.zh: 河水迅急，護之中流而下。

translations.literal: The river water was swift and urgent; Huzhi went downstream mid-river.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi rode the swift current downstream.

sentences.zh: 每至鐵鎖，以長柯斧斷之，魏不能禁；

translations.literal: Each time he reached iron chains, he used a long-handled axe to sever them — Wei could not stop him;
translations.idiomatic: At each chain he cut through with a long-handled axe. Wei could not stop him;

sentences.zh: 唯失一舸，餘皆完備而返。

translations.literal: Only one warship was lost; the rest all returned intact.
translations.idiomatic: He lost only one ship. The rest came back intact.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌遣沈慶之將五千人救玄謨，慶之曰：「玄謨士眾疲老，寇虜已逼，得數萬人乃可進。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin sent Shen Qingzhi with five thousand men to rescue Xuanmo; Shen Qingzhi said: "Xuanmo's troops and people are tired and old, the bandit barbarians already pressing close — one must have tens of thousands before one can advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin ordered Shen Qingzhi to take five thousand men to relieve Xuanmo. Qingzhi said, "Xuanmo's force is spent and the enemy is upon us — we need tens of thousands before we can move.

sentences.zh: 小軍輕往，無益也。」

translations.literal: A small army going lightly will be of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: A token force will do no good."

sentences.zh: 斌固遣之。

translations.literal: Bin still sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Bin sent him anyway.

sentences.zh: 會玄謨遁還，斌將斬之，慶之固諫曰：「佛狸威震天下，控弦百萬，豈玄謨所能當！

translations.literal: Meeting Xuanmo having fled back, Bin was about to behead him; Shen Qingzhi firmly remonstrated, saying: "Bili's might shakes the world, his bowstrings number a million — how could Xuanmo withstand him!
translations.idiomatic: Just then Xuanmo came running back. Bin was ready to execute him. Qingzhi intervened: "Bili's prestige fills the world and he commands a million archers — no one could have stood against him!

sentences.zh: 且殺戰將以自弱，非良計也。」

translations.literal: Moreover to kill a battle general and thereby weaken oneself is not a good plan."
translations.idiomatic: To kill your own commander in defeat would only weaken you further. That is no strategy at all."

sentences.zh: 斌乃止。

translations.literal: Bin then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Bin stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 斌欲固守碻磝，慶之曰：「今青、冀虛弱，而坐守窮城，若虜眾東過，清東非國家有也。

translations.literal: Bin wished to hold firm at Qiaoao; Shen Qingzhi said: "Now Qing and Ji are weak and empty, yet we sit guarding a trapped city — if the barbarian host passes eastward, the clear east will not belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Bin wanted to hold Qiaoao. Qingzhi said, "Qing and Ji are stripped bare. If we sit in this isolated stronghold while the enemy sweeps eastward, everything east of the clear lands will be lost.

sentences.zh: 碻敖磝孤絕，復作未修之滑台耳。」

translations.literal: Qiaoao, isolated and cut off, will again become the uncompleted Huatai."
translations.idiomatic: Qiaoao stands alone — no better than unfinished Huatai."

sentences.zh: 會詔使至，不聽斌等退師。

translations.literal: At that time an imperial envoy arrived, not permitting Bin and the rest to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: Just then an imperial messenger arrived forbidding Bin to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 斌復召諸將議之，江並謂宜留。

translations.literal: Bin again summoned the generals to discuss it; Jiang and the rest all held that they should stay.
translations.idiomatic: Bin called another council. Jiang and the others all argued to stay.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「閫外之事，將軍得以專之。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi said: "Matters outside the gate — the general may decide them alone.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "A commander in the field has authority to act on his own.

sentences.zh: 詔從遠來，不知事勢。

translations.literal: An edict coming from afar does not know the situation.
translations.idiomatic: An order from the capital knows nothing of conditions here.

sentences.zh: 節下有一范增不能用，空議何施！」

translations.literal: My lord has a Fan Zeng yet cannot use him — what use is empty discussion!"
translations.idiomatic: You have a Fan Zeng in your camp and will not heed him — of what use is all this talk?"

sentences.zh: 斌及坐者並笑曰：「沈公乃更學問！」

translations.literal: Bin and all those seated laughed together, saying: "Master Shen is displaying book learning again!"
translations.idiomatic: Bin and everyone present laughed. "Master Shen has been reading books again!"

sentences.zh: 慶之厲聲曰：「眾人雖知古今，不如下官耳學也。」

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi said in a harsh voice: "Though the crowd may know past and present, they are not the equal of this humble official's learning by ear."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi thundered back, "You may know history by heart, but none of you has the battle sense in my ears."

sentences.zh: 斌乃使王玄謨戍碻磝申坦，垣護之據清口，自帥諸軍還歷城。

translations.literal: Bin then assigned Wang Xuanmo to garrison Qiaoao, Shen Tan and Yuan Huzhi to hold Qingkou, and himself led the armies back to Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bin left Wang Xuanmo to hold Qiaoao, placed Shen Tan and Yuan Huzhi at Qingkou, and withdrew the main army to Licheng himself.

sentences.zh: 閏月，龐法起等諸軍入盧氏，斬縣令李封，以趙難為盧氏令，使帥其眾為鄉導。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, Pang Faqi's armies and the rest entered Lushi, beheaded Magistrate Li Feng, made Zhao Nan Lushi magistrate, and had him lead his people as local guides.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Pang Faqi's columns entered Lushi, executed magistrate Li Feng, installed Zhao Nan as magistrate, and used his followers as guides.

sentences.zh: 柳元景自百丈崖從諸軍於盧氏。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjing from Baihang Cliff followed the armies at Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing joined the force at Lushi by way of Baihang Cliff.

sentences.zh: 法起等進攻弘農，辛未，拔之，擒魏弘農太守李初古拔。

translations.literal: Faqi and the rest advanced to attack Hongnong; on xinwei day they took it and captured Wei Hongnong Prefect Li Chuguba.
translations.idiomatic: Faqi pressed the attack on Hongnong. On the day xinwei they took the city and captured Li Chuguba, Wei prefect of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 薛安都留屯弘農。

translations.literal: Xue Andu remained encamped at Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu stayed behind to hold Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，龐法起進向潼關。

translations.literal: On bingxu day, Pang Faqi advanced toward Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu, Pang Faqi marched on Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 魏主命諸將分道並進：永昌王仁自洛陽趨壽陽，尚書長孫真趣馬頭，楚王建趣鐘離，高涼王那自青州趣下邳，魏主自東平趣鄒山。

translations.literal: The Wei lord ordered the generals to advance separately on separate routes: Prince of Yongchang Ren from Luoyang hastened toward Shouyang, Minister Changsun Zhen hastened toward Matou, Prince of Chu Jian hastened toward Zhongli, Prince of Gaoliang Na from Qingzhou hastened toward Xiapi, and the Wei lord himself from Dongping hastened toward Zou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor divided his command. Prince Ren of Yongchang drove from Luoyang on Shouyang; Minister Changsun Zhen on Matou; Prince Jian of Chu on Zhongli; Prince Na of Gaoliang from Qingzhou on Xiapi; and the emperor himself marched from Dongping toward Mount Zou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛卯，魏主至鄒山，魯郡太守崔邪利為魏所擒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinmao day, the Wei lord reached Zou Mountain; Lu commandery Prefect Cui Xieli was captured by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day xinmao, the Wei emperor reached Mount Zou, where Cui Xieli, prefect of Lu commandery, was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 魏主見秦始皇石刻，使人排而僕之，以太牢祠孔子。

translations.literal: The Wei lord saw the stone inscriptions of Qin Shihuang, had men push them and topple them, and sacrificed with tai-lao to Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: At the site he ordered Qin Shihuang's stone inscriptions thrown down, then offered the grand sacrificial ox to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 楚王建自清西進，屯蕭城；

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Jian advanced from west of the Qing River and encamped at Xiaocheng;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Chu came up from west of the Qing and made camp at Xiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 步尼公自清東進，屯留城。

translations.literal: Bunigong advanced from east of the Qing and encamped at Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bunigong approached from the Qing's east bank and took position at Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 武陵王駿遣參軍馬文恭將兵向蕭城，江夏王義恭遣軍主嵇玄敬將兵向留城。

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling Jun sent Staff Officer Ma Wengong to lead troops toward Xiaocheng; Prince of Jiangxia Yigong sent Army Commander Ji Xuanjing to lead troops toward Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun of Wuling sent staff officer Ma Wengong against Xiaocheng; Prince Yigong of Jiangxia sent Ji Xuanjing, an army commander, against Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 文恭為魏所敗。

translations.literal: Wengong was defeated by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei forces routed Wengong.

sentences.zh: 步尼公遇玄敬，引兵趣苞橋，欲渡清西；

translations.literal: Bunigong encountered Xuanjing, led troops to hasten to Bao Bridge, wishing to cross west of the Qing;
translations.idiomatic: Bunigong met Xuanjing, then swung toward Bao Bridge to cross the Qing's west bank.

sentences.zh: 沛縣民燒苞橋，夜於林中擊鼓，魏以為宋兵大至，爭渡苞水，溺死者殆半。

translations.literal: The people of Pei county burned Bao Bridge; at night they beat drums in the forest; Wei thought Song troops had arrived in great numbers, competed to cross Bao water, and nearly half drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Pei county villagers burned the bridge and beat drums in the woods by night. The Wei troops, thinking a large Song force was upon them, scrambled to ford the Bao River — and nearly half drowned.

sentences.zh: 詔以柳元景為弘農太守。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Liu Yuanjing as Hongnong Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing was appointed prefect of Hongnong by imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 元景使薛安都、尹顯祖先引兵就龐法起等於陝，元景於後督租。

translations.literal: Yuanjing sent Xue Andu and Yin Xianzu ahead to lead troops to join Pang Faqi and others at Shan; Yuanjing in the rear supervised grain collection.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing sent Xue Andu and Yin Xianzu forward to link up with Pang Faqi at Shan, while he himself followed to levy grain supplies.

sentences.zh: 陝城險固，諸軍攻之不拔。

translations.literal: Shan city was perilous and solid; the armies attacked it but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was strongly fortified, and repeated assaults could not breach it.

sentences.zh: 魏洛州刺吏張是連提帥眾二萬度崤救陝，安都等與戰於城南，魏人縱突騎，諸軍不能敵；

translations.literal: Wei Luozhou Inspector Zhang Shilian led twenty thousand men across the Xiao Mountains to rescue Shan; Andu and others fought them south of the city; the Wei men released shock cavalry; the armies could not withstand them;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shilian, Wei inspector of Luozhou, led twenty thousand men over the Xiao Pass to relieve Shan. Andu and his colleagues met them south of the walls, but the Wei shock cavalry broke the Song line.

sentences.zh: 安都怒，脫兜鍪，解鎧，唯著絳納兩當衫，馬亦去具裝，瞋目橫矛，單騎突陳；

translations.literal: Andu grew angry, removed his helmet, undid his armor, wore only a crimson padded double-layered shirt, his horse also shed full barding, glared with eyes and held his spear crosswise, alone on horse charging the formation;
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Andu stripped off helmet and mail, leaving only a padded crimson vest — his horse likewise shed its barding — and with spear leveled and eyes blazing, charged alone into the enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 所向無前，魏人夾射不能中。

translations.literal: Wherever he went none could stand before him; the Wei men shot from both sides but could not hit him.
translations.idiomatic: He carved through without meeting resistance; arrows from both flanks failed to find him.

sentences.zh: 如是數四，殺傷不可勝數。

translations.literal: Thus four times, kills and wounds beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He repeated this charge four times, inflicting countless casualties.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，別將魯元保引兵自函谷關至，魏兵乃退。

translations.literal: At dusk, Separate General Lu Yuanbao led troops arriving from Hangu Pass, and the Wei troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Lu Yuanbao arrived from Hangu Pass with reinforcements, and the Wei army pulled back.

sentences.zh: 元景遣軍副柳元怙將步騎二千救安都等，夜至，魏人不之知。

translations.literal: Yuanjing sent Army Deputy Liu Yuanhu leading two thousand infantry and cavalry to rescue Andu and others; they arrived at night; the Wei men did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing dispatched his deputy Liu Yuanhu with two thousand horse and foot to Andu's aid. They arrived by night without the Wei camp's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 明日，安都等陳於城西南。

translations.literal: The next day, Andu and others drew up formation southwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning Andu's force deployed southwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 曾方平謂安都曰：「今勍敵在前，堅城在後，是吾取死之日。

translations.literal: Zeng Fangping said to Andu: "Now fierce enemies are before us, a solid city behind us — this is the day we seek death.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Fangping told Andu: "Formidable foes ahead, a fortress at our backs — today we fight as men who expect to die.

sentences.zh: 卿若不進，我當斬卿；

translations.literal: If you do not advance, I shall behead you;
translations.idiomatic: If you hold back, I will cut you down myself;

sentences.zh: 我若不進，卿斬我也！」

translations.literal: If I do not advance, you behead me!"
translations.idiomatic: and if I hold back, you may cut me down in turn!"

sentences.zh: 安都曰：「善，卿言是也！」

translations.literal: Andu said: "Good, your words are right!"
translations.idiomatic: Andu replied: "Well said — you are right!"

sentences.zh: 遂合戰。

translations.literal: Then they joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: And with that they closed in battle.

sentences.zh: 元怙引兵自南門鼓噪直出，旌旗甚盛，魏眾驚駭。

translations.literal: Yuanhu led troops straight out from the southern gate with drum and shout, banners and flags very grand; the Wei masses were startled and terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhu burst through the south gate with drums rolling and banners flying; the Wei ranks panicked.

sentences.zh: 安都挺身奮擊，流血凝肘，矛折，易之更入，諸軍齊奮。

translations.literal: Andu straightened his body and exerted fierce strikes; blood congealed at his elbows; his spear broke; he replaced it and entered again; all armies exerted together.
translations.idiomatic: Andu fought at the front until blood caked his elbows; when his spear snapped he seized another and plunged back in, and the whole line surged with him.

sentences.zh: 自旦至日昃，魏眾大潰，斬張是連提及將卒三千餘級。

translations.literal: From dawn to the slanting sun, the Wei masses greatly routed; Zhang Shilian was beheaded along with generals and soldiers numbering more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn until mid-afternoon the Wei army broke completely. Zhang Shilian fell, and more than three thousand officers and men with him.

sentences.zh: 其餘赴河塹死者甚眾，生降二千餘人。

translations.literal: The rest who rushed into the river ditch died in great numbers; more than two thousand surrendered alive.
translations.idiomatic: Countless others drowned in the river and moat; another two thousand surrendered.

sentences.zh: 明日，元景至，讓降者曰：「汝輩本中國民，今為虜盡力，力屈乃降，何也？」

translations.literal: The next day Yuanjing arrived and reproached the surrenderers: "You people were originally Chinese subjects; now you exert full strength for the barbarians; only when strength was exhausted did you surrender — why?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanjing arrived the next day, he upbraided the prisoners: "You are men of China. Why did you fight your hearts out for the enemy and surrender only when you could fight no more?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「「虜驅民使戰，後出者滅族，以騎蹙步，未戰先死，此將軍所親見也。」

translations.literal: All said: "The barbarians drive the people to fight; those who come out last have their clans extinguished; cavalry press upon infantry — before battle one already dies — this the general personally witnessed."
translations.idiomatic: They answered: "The Wei drive common folk into battle. Latecomers see their families wiped out; cavalry herd foot soldiers forward to die before a blow is struck — as you yourself saw."

sentences.zh: 諸將欲盡殺之，元景曰：「今王旗北指，當令仁聲先路。」

translations.literal: The generals wished to kill them all; Yuanjing said: "Now the royal banner points north; we ought to let benevolent reputation go before."
translations.idiomatic: Some officers wanted to execute them all, but Yuanjing said: "Our king's banner points north — let mercy go ahead of the army."

sentences.zh: 盡釋而遣之，皆稱萬歲而去。

translations.literal: All were released and sent away; all called "ten thousand years" and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He freed every man. They shouted their thanks and went home.

sentences.zh: 甲午，克陝城。

translations.literal: On jiawu day, Shan city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiawu, Shan fell.

sentences.zh: 龐法起等進攻潼關，魏戍主婁須棄城走，法起等據之。

translations.literal: Pang Faqi and others advanced to attack Tong Pass; Wei garrison commander Lou Xu abandoned the city and fled; Faqi and others occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Faqi pushed on Tong Pass. Lou Xu, the Wei garrison commander, fled, and Faqi seized the pass.

sentences.zh: 關中豪桀所在蜂起，及四山羌、胡皆來送款。

translations.literal: Powerful men of Guanzhong rose everywhere like bees; and Qiang and Hu of the four mountains all came to offer allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong magnates rebelled on every side; Qiang and Hu tribes from the surrounding hills came in to pledge loyalty.

sentences.zh: 上以王玄謨敗退，魏兵深入，柳元景等不宜獨進，皆召還。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Wang Xuanmo had been defeated and withdrawn and Wei troops had penetrated deeply, considered Liu Yuanjing and others unsuitable for advancing alone, and all were summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Xuanmo's defeat and the Wei's deep advance, the emperor judged that Yuanjing could not press forward alone and recalled the western columns.

sentences.zh: 元景使薛安都斷後，引兵歸襄陽。

translations.literal: Yuanjing sent Xue Andu to cover the rear and led troops back to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing left Xue Andu to guard the retreat and withdrew to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 詔以元景為襄陽太守。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yuanjing as Xiangyang Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was made prefect of Xiangyang by decree.

sentences.zh: 魏永昌王仁攻懸瓠、項城，拔之。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Yongchang Ren attacked Xuanhu and Xiangcheng and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ren of Yongchang took Xuanhu and Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 帝恐魏兵至壽陽，召劉康祖使還。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing Wei troops would reach Shouyang, summoned Liu Kangzu to return.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Wei would reach Shouyang, the emperor called Liu Kangzu back.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，仁將八萬騎追及康祖於尉武。

translations.literal: On guimao day, Ren with eighty thousand cavalry caught up with Kangzu at Yuwu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao, Ren overtook Kangzu at Yuwu with eighty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 康祖有眾八千人，軍副胡盛之欲依山險間行取至，康祖怒曰：「臨河求敵，遂無所見；

translations.literal: Kangzu had eight thousand men; Army Deputy Hu Shengzhi wished to take a hidden route through mountain peril; Kangzu angrily said: "We came to the river seeking the enemy and found nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu had only eight thousand men. His deputy Hu Shengzhi urged slipping through the hills by a hidden path, but Kangzu snapped: "We marched to the river looking for a fight and found none.

sentences.zh: 幸其自送，奈何避之！」

translations.literal: Fortunately they deliver themselves — how can we avoid them!
translations.idiomatic: Now they have delivered themselves — and you would run from them?"

sentences.zh: 乃結車營而進，下令軍中曰：「顧望者斬首，轉步者斬足！」

translations.literal: Then he formed a wagon camp and advanced, issuing an order in the army: "Those who look back — behead; those who turn their steps — cut off the feet!"
translations.idiomatic: He formed a wagon laager and advanced, ordering: "Look back and lose your head; step aside and lose your feet!"

sentences.zh: 魏人四面攻之，將士皆殊死戰。

translations.literal: The Wei men attacked from four sides; generals and soldiers all fought to special death.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei attacked from all sides; every man fought as if his life were already forfeit.

sentences.zh: 自旦至晡，殺魏兵萬餘人，流血沒踝，康祖身被十創，意氣彌厲。

translations.literal: From dawn to shen hour they killed Wei troops more than ten thousand; blood drowned the ankles; Kangzu's body received ten wounds; his spirit grew even fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn to mid-afternoon they killed more than ten thousand Wei soldiers. Blood stood ankle-deep. Kangzu took ten wounds and fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 魏分其眾為三，且休且戰。

translations.literal: Wei divided their masses into three, resting and fighting alternately.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei split into three relays, fighting and resting in turns.

sentences.zh: 會日暮風急，魏以騎負草燒車營，康祖隨補其闕。

translations.literal: At dusk wind blew fierce; Wei used cavalry carrying grass to burn the wagon camp; Kangzu as he went patched its gaps.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a gale rose. Wei horsemen piled grass against the wagons and set them ablaze while Kangzu raced to plug every breach.

sentences.zh: 有流矢貫康祖頸，墜馬死，餘眾不能戰，遂潰，魏人掩殺殆盡。

translations.literal: A stray arrow pierced Kangzu's neck; he fell from horse and died; the remaining masses could not fight; then they routed; Wei men covered and killed nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow took Kangzu in the throat. He fell dead from his horse. The rest broke and were cut down almost to the last man.

sentences.zh: 南平王鑠使左軍行參軍王羅漢以三百人戍尉武。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanping Shuo sent Left Army Acting Staff Officer Wang Luohan with three hundred men to garrison Yuwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuo of Nanping posted staff officer Wang Luohan at Yuwu with three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 魏兵至，眾欲南依卑林以自固，羅漢以受命居此，不去。

translations.literal: When Wei troops arrived, the masses wished to rely on Beilin to the south to secure themselves; Luohan, having received orders to hold this place, did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei arrived, his men wanted to retreat into the southern woods for safety, but Luohan refused to abandon the post he had been given.

sentences.zh: 魏人攻而擒之，鎖其頸，使三郎將掌之；

translations.literal: The Wei men attacked and captured him, locked his neck, and had a third-rank general guard him;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei stormed the position, seized him, clamped an iron collar around his neck, and put a third-rank officer in charge of him.

sentences.zh: 羅漢夜斷三郎將首，抱鎖亡奔盱眙。

translations.literal: Luohan at night cut off the third-rank general's head, embraced the lock and fled, running to Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: That night Luohan killed his guard, still wearing the collar, and fled to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 魏永昌王仁進逼壽陽，焚掠馬頭、鐘離，南平王鑠嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Yongchang Ren pressed forward toward Shouyang, burning and plundering Matou and Zhongli; Prince of Nanping Shuo defended the city closely and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ren of Yongchang pushed on Shouyang, burning Matou and Zhongli as he came. Prince Shuo of Nanping barricaded himself inside the walls and held on.

sentences.zh: 魏軍在蕭城，支彭城十餘里。

translations.literal: Wei armies were at Xiaocheng, ten-odd li from Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops camped at Xiaocheng, a dozen li from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 彭城兵雖多，而食少，太尉江夏王義恭欲棄彭城南歸。

translations.literal: Though Pengcheng's troops were many, food was few; Grand Marshal Prince of Jiangxia Yigong wished to abandon Pengcheng and return south.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng had plenty of soldiers but little grain. Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia wanted to abandon the city and flee south.

sentences.zh: 安北中兵參軍沈慶之以為歷城兵少食多，欲為函箱車陳，以精兵為外翼，奉二王及妃女直趨歷城；

translations.literal: Pacifying the North Central Troops Staff Officer Shen Qingzhi considered Licheng had few troops and much food; he wished to form a covered-wagon formation, with elite troops as outer wings, escorting the two princes and consorts and daughters straight to Licheng;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi, Pacifying the North central staff officer, argued for Licheng — fewer defenders, more provisions — and proposed a wagon-fort formation with crack troops on the flanks to escort the two princes and the royal women straight to Licheng.

sentences.zh: 分兵配護軍蕭思話，使留守彭城。

translations.literal: Dividing troops and assigning Protector of the Army Xiao Sihua, he had him remain to hold Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: A detachment under Protector of the Army Xiao Sihua would stay behind to hold Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 太尉長史何勖欲席捲奔郁洲，自海道還京師。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Chief of Staff He Xu wished to sweep everything and flee to Yuzhou, returning to the capital by sea route.
translations.idiomatic: Grand marshal chief of staff He Xu favored abandoning everything and running to Yuzhou, then taking ship home to the capital.

sentences.zh: 義恭去意已判。

translations.literal: Yigong's intention to leave was already decided.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong's mind was made up to go.

sentences.zh: 唯二議彌日未決。

translations.literal: Only the two proposals were debated day-long without decision.
translations.idiomatic: The two plans were argued back and forth all day without resolution.

sentences.zh: 安北長史沛郡太守張暢曰：「若歷城、郁洲有可至之理，下官敢不高贊！

translations.literal: Pacifying the North Chief of Staff Pei Commandery Prefect Zhang Chang said: "If Licheng and Yuzhou had paths that could be reached, this subordinate would dare not fail to endorse highly!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang, Pacifying the North chief of staff and prefect of Pei commandery, said: "If Licheng or Yuzhou were truly reachable, I would be the first to urge it.

sentences.zh: 今城中乏食，百姓鹹有走志，但以關扃嚴固，欲去莫從耳。

translations.literal: Now within the city food is scarce; common people all have the will to flee, but only because the gates and bars are strictly secured, wishing to go they have no one to follow.
translations.idiomatic: But the city is short of food, and every civilian wants to run — they stay only because the gates are barred tight and no one leads the way.

sentences.zh: 一旦動足，則各自逃散，欲至所在，何由可得！

translations.literal: Once feet move, then each flees and scatters separately; wishing to reach the place intended, how could it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: The moment we stir, everyone will scatter on his own. None of us will reach whatever destination you have in mind.

sentences.zh: 今軍食是寡，朝夕猶未窘罄；

translations.literal: Now army provisions though few, morning and evening have still not reached utter depletion;
translations.idiomatic: Our stores are thin, but we are not yet starving;

sentences.zh: 豈有捨萬安之術而就危亡之道？

translations.literal: How can there be abandoning a ten-thousand-fold secure method and taking a perilous ruinous path?
translations.idiomatic: why trade a strategy that might yet save us for one that guarantees disaster?

sentences.zh: 若此計必行，下官請以頸血污公馬蹄。」

translations.literal: If this plan must be carried out, this subordinate asks to use neck blood to stain the lord's horse hooves.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on this plan, I ask only to die under your horse's hooves."

sentences.zh: 武陵王駿謂義恭曰：「阿父既為總統，去留非所敢干，道民忝為城主，而委鎮奔逃，實無顏復奉朝廷。

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling Jun said to Yigong: "Uncle-father already serves as supreme commander; going or staying is not what I dare interfere in; Daomin humbly serves as city lord, yet to abandon the fortification and flee — truly no face to again serve the court.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun of Wuling told Yigong: "You command this army — I would not presume to tell you whether to stay or go. But I am lord of this city. If I abandon my post and flee, I will have no face left to serve the court again.

sentences.zh: 必與此城共其存沒，張長史言不可異也。」

translations.literal: I must with this city share its survival and destruction; Chief of Staff Zhang's words cannot be made different.
translations.idiomatic: I will live or die with Pengcheng. Chief of Staff Zhang speaks for me as well."

sentences.zh: 義恭乃止。

translations.literal: Yigong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong gave up the idea of flight.

sentences.zh: 壬子，魏主至彭城，立氈屋於戲馬台以望城中。

translations.literal: On renzi day, the Wei lord reached Pengcheng, erecting felt tents at Ximat Platform to observe the city within.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renzi the Wei emperor reached Pengcheng and pitched felt tents on the Horse-Training Terrace to survey the city.

sentences.zh: 馬文恭之敗也，隊主蒯應沒於魏。

translations.literal: When Ma Wengong was defeated, squad leader Kuai Ying was lost to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Wengong was routed, squad leader Kuai Ying fell into Wei hands.

sentences.zh: 魏主遣應至小市門求酒及甘蔗；

translations.literal: The Wei lord sent Ying to the Small Market Gate to request wine and sugarcane;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent Ying to the Small Market Gate to ask for wine and sugarcane.

sentences.zh: 武陵王駿與之，仍就求橐駝。

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling Jun gave them to him, and he again requested camels.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun of Wuling obliged him — whereupon Ying asked for camels as well.

sentences.zh: 明日，魏主使尚書李孝伯至南門，餉義恭貂裘，餉駿橐駝及騾，且曰：「魏主致意安北，可暫出見我；

translations.literal: The next day the Wei lord sent Minister Li Xiaobo to the South Gate, presenting Yigong a sable fur coat, presenting Jun camels and mules, and saying: "The Wei lord sends regards to Pacifying the North — you may briefly come out to see me;
translations.idiomatic: The next day Minister Li Xiaobo came to the south gate with a sable coat for Yigong, camels and mules for Jun, and a message: "The emperor sends his regards to Pacifying the North. Step out briefly and meet me.

sentences.zh: 我亦不攻此城，何為勞苦將士，備守如此！」

translations.literal: I also will not attack this city — why labor and toil the generals and soldiers, preparing defense so thoroughly!
translations.idiomatic: I do not intend to storm this city — why wear your men out with such exhausting defenses?"

sentences.zh: 駿使張暢開門出見之，曰：「安北致意魏主，常遲面寫，但以人臣無境外之交，恨不暫悉。

translations.literal: Jun sent Zhang Chang to open the gate and go out to see him, saying: "Pacifying the North sends regards to the Wei lord, always deferred face-to-face meeting, but as a subject-minister there is no contact beyond the border — regret not briefly knowing fully.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Zhang Chang out through the gate to reply: "Pacifying the North sends his regards. He would gladly meet you in person, but a subject may not treat abroad; he regrets only that acquaintance must stop at the frontier.

sentences.zh: 備守乃邊鎮之常，悅以使之，則勞而無怨耳。」

translations.literal: Preparing defense is the constant of border fortifications; if pleased to employ them thus, then labor but without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison duty is the border soldier's trade — keep him busy and he complains less."

sentences.zh: 魏主求甘橘及借博具，皆與之；

translations.literal: The Wei lord requested sweet oranges and to borrow gaming pieces; all were given;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor asked for sweet oranges and loan of gaming boards; both were sent out.

sentences.zh: 復餉氈及九種鹽胡豉。

translations.literal: Again presented were felt and nine kinds of salt, Hu fermented beans.
translations.idiomatic: Felt rugs followed, and nine varieties of salt and fermented bean paste.

sentences.zh: 又借樂器，義恭應之曰：「受任戎行，不繼樂具。」

translations.literal: Again borrowed musical instruments; Yigong replied: "Having received appointment on the military march, no musical instruments were brought along."
translations.idiomatic: When they asked to borrow musicians, Yigong answered: "We marched to war, not to concert."

sentences.zh: 孝伯問暢：「何為匆匆閉門絕橋？」

translations.literal: Xiaobo asked Chang: "Why urgently close gates and cut off bridges?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo asked Chang: "Why were the gates slammed shut and the bridges drawn so hastily?"

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「二王以魏主營壘未立，將士疲勞。

translations.literal: Chang said: "The two princes considered the Wei lord's camps and ramparts not yet established, generals and soldiers weary.
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied: "The two princes noticed your camp was not yet set and your men were weary.

sentences.zh: 此精甲十萬，恐輕相陵踐，故閉城耳。

translations.literal: These fine armors ten thousand — fearing lightly mutual bullying and trampling — therefore closed the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand elite armored troops might stampede one another — so we kept the gates shut.

sentences.zh: 待休息士馬，然後共治戰場，刻日交戲。」

translations.literal: Wait until troops and horses rest, then together fix the battlefield, set a day for mutual contest.
translations.idiomatic: Let men and horses recover, and we can fix a day to meet properly on the field."

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「賓有禮，主則擇之。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "When the guest has ritual, the host then selects."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo answered: "When the guest shows courtesy, the host may choose his company."

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「昨見眾賓至門，未為有禮。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "Yesterday seeing the multitude of guests reach the gate — not yet ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "Yesterday your guests reached our gate without the least courtesy."

sentences.zh: 魏主使人來言曰：「致意太尉、安北，何不遣人來至我所？

translations.literal: The Wei lord sent men to say: "Send regards to Grand Marshal and Pacifying the North — why not dispatch men to come to my place?
translations.idiomatic: An envoy from the Wei emperor asked: "Give our regards to the Grand Marshal and Pacifying the North — why not send someone to our camp?

sentences.zh: 彼此之情，雖不可盡。

translations.literal: Each other's feelings, though cannot be fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: Feelings between us cannot be conveyed entirely in letters.

sentences.zh: 要須見我小大，知我老小，觀我為人。

translations.literal: Essentially must see my size, know my old and young, observe my conduct as a person.
translations.idiomatic: I must be seen in person — my stature, my age, my character.

sentences.zh: 若諸佐不可遣，亦可使僮幹來。」

translations.literal: If the various aides cannot be dispatched, one may also send servant attendants.
translations.idiomatic: If your chief officers cannot come, send a clerk."

sentences.zh: 暢以二王命對曰：「魏主形狀才力，久為來往所具。

translations.literal: Chang on the two princes' orders replied: "The Wei lord's form and strength, long ago fully known through mutual visits.
translations.idiomatic: Chang answered for both princes: "Your stature and prowess are well known from long exchange across the border.

sentences.zh: 李尚書親自銜命，不患彼此不盡，故不復遣使。」

translations.literal: Minister Li personally bears the mandate; no worry that each side cannot express fully — therefore no further envoys are dispatched."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li carries your message in person — nothing left unsaid — so there is no need for another envoy."

sentences.zh: 孝伯又曰：「王玄謨亦常才耳，南國何意作如此任使，以致奔敗？

translations.literal: Xiaobo again said: "Wang Xuanmo is also merely ordinary talent — what did the southern state intend in making such an appointment and deployment, to cause routed defeat?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo pressed on: "Wang Xuanmo is nothing special. Why did your court place such a man in command and bring on this rout?

sentences.zh: 自入此境七百餘里，主人竟不能一相拒逆。

translations.literal: Since entering this territory more than seven hundred li, the host actually could not once resist and oppose.
translations.idiomatic: We have marched seven hundred li into your land without a single real stand.

sentences.zh: 鄒山之險，君家所憑，前鋒始接，崔邪利遽藏入穴，諸將倒曳出之。

translations.literal: Zou Mountain's peril — your family's reliance — the vanguard had barely joined; Cui Xieli hurriedly hid in a cave; the generals dragged him out upside down.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Zou, your own stronghold, your prefect Cui Xieli hid in a cave the moment our van arrived. Your own generals had to drag him out feet first.

sentences.zh: 魏主賜其餘生，今從在此。」

translations.literal: The Wei lord granted him remaining life; now he follows here."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared his life — and he is here with us now."

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「王玄謨南土偏將，不謂為才，但以之為前驅，大軍未至，河冰向合，玄謨因夜還軍，致戎馬小亂耳。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Wang Xuanmo is a southern territory peripheral general, not considered talented; only using him as vanguard, the great army had not arrived, the river ice was about to join, Xuanmo therefore by night returned the army, causing military horses a small disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied: "Wang Xuanmo is a minor southern commander — nobody rated him highly. He was sent ahead as vanguard. The main force had not yet arrived, the river was about to freeze, and he withdrew by night — a trifling disorder of horse and camp, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 崔邪利陷沒，何損於國！

translations.literal: Cui Xieli fell and was captured — what harm to the state!
translations.idiomatic: What does it matter if Cui Xieli was taken? It is no loss to our state!

sentences.zh: 魏主自以數十萬眾制一崔邪利，乃足言邪！

translations.literal: The Wei lord himself uses several hundred thousand masses to control one Cui Xieli — is that worth speaking of!
translations.idiomatic: That your emperor needed hundreds of thousands of men to deal with one prefect — is that truly something to boast of?

sentences.zh: 知入境七百里無相拒者，此自太尉神算，鎮軍聖略，用兵有機，不用相語。」

translations.literal: Knowing that entering the border seven hundred li had none to resist — this is itself the Grand Marshal's divine calculation and the Pacifying Army's sage strategy; employing troops has its timing — no need to speak of it to each other."
translations.idiomatic: As for marching seven hundred li without meeting real resistance — that reflects the Grand Marshal's shrewd planning and the Pacifying Army's strategy. There is art in deploying troops; we need not discuss it further."

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「魏主當不圍此城，自帥眾軍直造瓜步。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "The Wei lord likely will not besiege this city; he himself will lead the mass of armies straight to Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "The Wei emperor will probably not linger here. He will lead his main force straight to Guabu.

sentences.zh: 南事若辦，彭城不待圍；

translations.literal: If the southern affair succeeds, Pengcheng need not await siege;
translations.idiomatic: If his southern campaign succeeds, Pengcheng will fall without a siege;

sentences.zh: 若其不捷，彭城亦非所須也。

translations.literal: If it does not succeed, Pengcheng also is not what is needed.
translations.idiomatic: and if it fails, he will not need Pengcheng at all.

sentences.zh: 我今當南飲江湖以療渴耳。」

translations.literal: I now shall go south to drink the rivers and lakes to cure thirst, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I mean only to ride south and drink from your rivers to slake my thirst."

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「去留之事，自適彼懷。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Matters of going and staying — let them suit his own heart.
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied, "Whether you stay or go is entirely your choice.

sentences.zh: 若虜馬遂得飲江，便為無復天道。」

translations.literal: If the barbarian horses then obtain to drink the river, then there would be no more Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: But if barbarian horses truly drink from the Yangtze, that will mean Heaven itself has abandoned us."

sentences.zh: 先是童謠云：「虜馬飲江水，佛狸死卯年。」

translations.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme said: "Barbarian horses drink river water; Bilü dies in a mao year."
translations.idiomatic: A children's rhyme had said: "When the barbarian horses drink the river, Bilü will die in a Mao year."

sentences.zh: 故暢云然。

translations.literal: Therefore Chang spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Chang said what he did.

sentences.zh: 暢音容雅麗，孝伯與左右皆歎息。

translations.literal: Chang's voice and bearing were elegant and fine; Xiaobo and those at his side all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's voice and bearing were refined and graceful; Xiaobo and his attendants all sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 孝伯亦辯贍，且去，謂暢曰：「長史深自愛，相去步武，恨不執手。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo was also eloquent and resourceful; as he was about to leave he said to Chang: "Chief Administrator, take good care of yourself. We are only a few paces apart — I regret we cannot clasp hands."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo was quick and eloquent himself. As he took leave he said to Chang, "Chief Administrator, take care. We stand only steps apart, yet I regret we cannot shake hands."

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「君善自愛，冀蕩定有期，相見無遠。

translations.literal: Chang said: "My lord, take good care of yourself. I hope pacification and settlement will have a fixed time; our meeting will not be far off.
translations.idiomatic: Chang answered, "You too must take care. I hope the realm will be settled ere long; we shall meet again before long.

sentences.zh: 君若得還宋期，今為相識之始」。

translations.literal: If you can return to the Song capital in due course, today marks the beginning of acquaintance."
translations.idiomatic: If you live to see the Song capital again, let today be the day we first knew each other."

sentences.zh: 上起楊文德為輔國將軍，引兵自漢中西入，搖動汧、隴。

translations.literal: The emperor raised Yang Wende to Aiding-the-State General, leading troops from Hanzhong westward in, shaking Qian and Long.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor restored Yang Wende as Aiding-the-State General and sent him west from Hanzhong to stir up Qian and Long.

sentences.zh: 文德宗人楊高帥陰平、平武群氐拒之。

translations.literal: Yang Wende's clansman Yang Gao led the Di groups of Yinping and Pingwu to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gao, a kinsman of Wende's clan, rallied the Di of Yinping and Pingwu against him.

sentences.zh: 文德擊高，斬之，陰平、平武悉平。

translations.literal: Wende attacked Gao, beheaded him; Yinping and Pingwu were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wende attacked Gao, killed him, and pacified Yinping and Pingwu entirely.

sentences.zh: 梁、南秦二州刺史劉秀之遣文德伐啖提氐，不克，執送荊州；

translations.literal: Liang and Southern Qin the two prefecture inspectors Liu Xiuzhi dispatched Wende to attack the Dianti Di; he did not succeed, was seized and sent to Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuzhi, inspector of Liang and Southern Qin, then sent Wende against the Dianti Di. He failed and was arrested and sent to Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 使文德從祖兄頭戍葭蘆。

translations.literal: He had Wende's elder cousin from the same clan Tou garrison Jialu.
translations.idiomatic: Tou, Wende's elder cousin from the same clan, was put in charge of Jialu.

sentences.zh: 丁未，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingwei, general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏主攻彭城，不克。

translations.literal: The Wei lord attacked Pengcheng and did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor besieged Pengcheng but failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙辰朔，引兵南下，使中書郎魯秀出廣陵，高涼王那出山陽，永昌王仁出橫江，所過無不殘滅，城邑皆望風奔潰。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day of the cycle beginning bingchen, he led troops south; he sent Palace Gentleman Lu Xiu toward Guangling, Prince of Gaoliang Na out from Shanyang, Prince of Yongchang Ren out from Hengjiang — wherever they passed none escaped devastation; cities and towns all fled at the wind.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the new-moon day bingchen, he marched south. He sent Palace Attendant Lu Xiu toward Guangling, Prince of Gaoliang Na from Shanyang, and Prince of Yongchang Ren from Hengjiang. Everywhere they passed they left ruin; towns surrendered or fled at their approach.

sentences.zh: 戊午，建康纂嚴。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Jiankang assembled strictness.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day martial law was declared in Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 己未，魏兵至淮上。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Wei troops reached the Huai bank.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day Wei forces reached the Huai.

sentences.zh: 上使輔國將軍臧質將萬人救彭城。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Aiding-the-State General Zang Zhi to command ten thousand men to rescue Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Aiding-the-State General Zang Zhi with ten thousand men to relieve Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 至盱眙，魏主已過淮。

translations.literal: When he reached Xuyi, the Wei lord had already crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Xuyi, the Wei emperor had already crossed the Huai.

sentences.zh: 質使冗從僕射胡崇之、積弩將軍臧澄之營東山，建威將軍毛熙祚據前浦，質營於城南。

translations.literal: Zhi had Supernumerary Attendant Hu Chongzhi and Strongbow General Zang Chengzhi encamp at East Hill, Establishing Might General Mao Xizuo hold the forward ford, and Zhi encamped south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi posted Supernumerary Attendant Hu Chongzhi and Strongbow General Zang Chengzhi on East Hill, had Establishing Might General Mao Xizuo hold the forward ford, and made his own camp south of the city.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏燕王譚攻崇之等三營，皆敗沒，質案兵不敢救。

translations.literal: On yichou, Wei Prince of Yan Tan attacked the three camps of Chongzhi and the others — all were defeated and destroyed; Zhi held his troops and dared not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day Prince of Yan Tan of Wei attacked all three camps; every detachment was overrun. Zhi kept his main force still and dared not intervene.

sentences.zh: 澄之，燾之孫；

translations.literal: Chengzhi was Tao's grandson;
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi was a grandson of Zang Tao;

sentences.zh: 熙祚，修之之兄子也。

translations.literal: Xizuo was Xiuzhi's brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xizuo was a nephew of Mao Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 是夕，質軍亦潰，質棄輜重器械，單將七百人赴城。

translations.literal: That evening Zhi's army also collapsed; Zhi abandoned baggage train and equipment, alone leading seven hundred men toward the city.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhi's army broke as well. He abandoned supplies and weapons and entered the city with only seven hundred men.

sentences.zh: 初，盱眙太守沈璞到官，王玄謨猶在滑台，江淮無警。

translations.literal: Initially, when Xuyi Prefect Shen Pu took office, Wang Xuanmo was still at Huatai; the Jiang and Huai had no alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Pu first took office as prefect of Xuyi, Wang Xuanmo was still holding Huatai and the Jiang-Huai region was quiet.
