sentences.zh: 璞以郡當衝要，乃繕城浚隍，積財谷，儲矢石，為城守之備。

translations.literal: Pu considered the commandery on a critical juncture; therefore he repaired walls, dredged moats, accumulated wealth and grain, stored arrows and stones, making preparations for holding the city.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his district lay on a vital route, he repaired the walls, deepened the moat, stockpiled grain and wealth, and stored arrows and stones for a siege.

sentences.zh: 僚屬皆非之，朝廷亦以為過。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials all disapproved; the court also considered it excessive.
translations.idiomatic: His staff objected, and the court likewise thought him excessive.

sentences.zh: 及魏兵南向，守宰多棄城走。

translations.literal: When Wei troops turned south, defending officials mostly abandoned cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei armies marched south, most local officials fled their posts.

sentences.zh: 或勸璞宜還建康，璞曰：「虜若以城小不顧，夫復何懼！

translations.literal: Some urged Pu that he should return to Jiankang; Pu said: "If the barbarians, because the city is small, do not attend to it, what further fear!
translations.idiomatic: Some advised him to withdraw to Jiankang. Pu said, "If the enemy ignores us because the town is small, what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 若肉薄來攻，此乃吾報國之秋，諸君封侯之日也，奈何去之！

translations.literal: If they press close to attack, this is my season to repay the state, the day for you all to be enfeoffed as marquises — how can we leave!
translations.idiomatic: If they press in close and storm the walls, this is my chance to serve the realm and your chance to win marquisates — why would we run?

sentences.zh: 諸君嘗見數十萬人聚於小城之下而不敗者乎？

translations.literal: Have you ever seen several hundred thousand men gathered beneath a small city and not be defeated?
translations.idiomatic: Have you ever seen hundreds of thousands fail to take a small city?

sentences.zh: 昆陽、合肥，前事之明驗也。」

translations.literal: Kunyang and Hefei — clear proof from former events.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyang and Hefei are proof enough.

sentences.zh: 眾心稍定。

translations.literal: The crowd's hearts gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: The men's spirits steadied somewhat.

sentences.zh: 璞收集得二千精兵，曰：「足矣！」

translations.literal: Pu gathered and obtained two thousand elite troops and said: "Enough!
translations.idiomatic: Pu mustered two thousand picked men and said, "That is enough!

sentences.zh: 及臧質向城，眾謂璞曰：「虜若不攻城，則無所事眾；

translations.literal: When Zang Zhi approached the city, the crowd said to Pu: "If the barbarians do not attack the city, there is nothing to do with the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi came to the city, his men told Pu, "If the enemy does not besiege us, so many men are useless;

sentences.zh: 若其攻城，則城中止可容見力耳。

translations.literal: If they attack the city, then within the city only visible strength can be accommodated.
translations.idiomatic: if they do attack, the city can only hold those needed to fight.

sentences.zh: 地狹人多，鮮不為患。

translations.literal: The ground narrow, people many — rarely would it not become a hazard.
translations.idiomatic: Cramped quarters and too many men will only cause trouble.

sentences.zh: 且敵眾我寡，人所共知，若以質眾能退敵完城者，則全功不在我；

translations.literal: Moreover the enemy numerous, we few — what people jointly know — if with Zhi's multitude they can repel the enemy and complete the city, then the full achievement is not with us;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, everyone knows we are outnumbered. If Zhi's troops drive the enemy off and save the city, we will get no credit;

sentences.zh: 若避罪歸都，會資舟楫，必更相蹂踐。

translations.literal: If to avoid blame they return to the capital, meeting to provision boats — necessarily they will further trample one another.
translations.idiomatic: and if they flee south to escape blame, they will crowd the boats and trample one another to death.

sentences.zh: 正足為患，不若閉門勿受。」

translations.literal: That is exactly enough to become a hazard; better close the gates and not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: That would be a disaster. Better keep the gates shut."

sentences.zh: 璞歎曰：「虜必不能登城，敢為諸君保之。

translations.literal: Pu sighed and said: "The barbarians surely cannot ascend the city — I dare guarantee it for you all.
translations.idiomatic: Pu sighed. "The enemy cannot take this city — I'll warrant it.

sentences.zh: 舟楫之計，固已久息，虜之殘害，古今未有，屠剝之苦，眾所共見，其中幸者，不過得驅還北國作奴婢耳。

translations.literal: The plan of boats — long since ceased; the barbarians' devastation, in antiquity and today never seen; the suffering of slaughter and flaying, what the multitude jointly sees — among them the fortunate, at most can be driven back to the northern state to become slave girls and servants.
translations.idiomatic: Forget any idea of escape by boat. Their savagery is unmatched. You have all seen the slaughter. The lucky ones become slaves in the north.

sentences.zh: 彼雖烏合，寧不憚此邪！

translations.literal: Though they are a rabble gathered, would they not fear this!
translations.idiomatic: Even a rabble army must dread that fate!

sentences.zh: 所謂『同舟而濟，胡、越一心』者也。

translations.literal: What is called "sharing one boat to cross — Hu and Yue of one heart."
translations.idiomatic: This is what people mean when they say, 'Men in the same boat pull together, though they be Hu and Yue.'

sentences.zh: 今兵多則虜退速，少則退緩。

translations.literal: Now if troops many, then the barbarians retreat quickly; if few, then retreat slowly.
translations.idiomatic: More men will make the enemy leave sooner; fewer will slow them down a little.

sentences.zh: 吾寧可欲專功而留虜乎！」

translations.literal: How could I wish to monopolize achievement and keep the barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: Would I hoard the credit and keep the enemy here longer?

sentences.zh: 乃開門納質。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened the gates and admitted Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: So he opened the gates and admitted Zhi.

sentences.zh: 質見城中豐實，大喜，眾皆稱萬歲，因與璞共守。

translations.literal: Zhi saw the city abundant and full — greatly rejoiced; the multitude all shouted "Ten thousand years"; therefore he and Pu jointly defended.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi found the city well stocked and rejoiced. The soldiers cheered. He and Pu defended together.

sentences.zh: 魏人之南寇也，不繼糧用，唯以抄掠為資。

translations.literal: When Wei people raided south, they did not carry forward grain supplies — only taking plunder as resources.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei invaders brought no supply train; they lived by plunder alone.

sentences.zh: 及過淮，民多竄匿，抄掠無所得，人馬饑乏；

translations.literal: When they crossed the Huai, the people mostly hid in flight; plunder obtained nothing; men and horses hungered and lacked.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Huai the people hid themselves; raids yielded nothing; men and horses grew hungry and weary;

sentences.zh: 聞盱眙有積粟，欲以為北歸之資。

translations.literal: Hearing Xuyi had accumulated grain, they wished to make it resources for returning north.
translations.idiomatic: hearing that Xuyi had stored grain, they meant to seize it for the march home.

sentences.zh: 既破崇之等，一攻城不拔，即留其將韓元興以數千人守盱眙，自帥大眾南向。

translations.literal: Having already defeated Chongzhi and the others, once attacking the city they could not take it — immediately he left his general Han Yuanxing with several thousand men to hold Xuyi, himself leading the great multitude south.
translations.idiomatic: After crushing Chongzhi's detachment they assaulted the city once and failed. The Wei emperor left Han Yuanxing with a few thousand men to blockade Xuyi and marched on south with his main force.

sentences.zh: 由是盱眙得益完守備。

translations.literal: By this Xuyi obtained further complete defensive preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyi thus had even more time to prepare its defenses.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏主至瓜步，壞民廬舍，及伐葦為筏，聲言欲渡江。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Wei lord reached Guabu, destroyed people's houses, and moreover cut reeds to make rafts, declaring by word that he wished to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day the Wei emperor reached Guabu, demolished dwellings, cut reeds for rafts, and announced that he would cross the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 建康震懼，民皆荷擔而立。

translations.literal: Jiankang was shaken with fear; the people all stood with carrying poles on their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang panicked; people stood ready with packs on their shoulders to flee.

sentences.zh: 壬午，內外戒嚴，丹陽統內盡戶發丁，王公以下子弟皆從役。

translations.literal: On renwu, inside and outside were on strict alert; within Danyang jurisdiction every household sent levies; from public kings and dukes downward, sons and younger brothers all followed service.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day full martial law was declared. Every household in Danyang was mobilized; sons of the nobility down to common families were conscripted.

sentences.zh: 命領軍將軍劉遵考等將兵分守津要，游邏上接於湖，下至蔡洲，陳艦列營，周亙江濱。

translations.literal: He ordered Commanding General Liu Zunkao and others to lead troops separately guarding ford passes; patrols upstream reached Yu Lake, downstream to Caizhou — deploying ships and arraying camps, encircling the river bank.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Commanding General Liu Zunkao and others to hold the fords. Patrol boats ranged from Lake Yu upstream to Cai Isle downstream; warships and camps lined the river for miles.

sentences.zh: 自採石至於暨陽，六七百里。

translations.literal: From Caishi to Jiyang — six or seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: From Caishi to Jiyang — six or seven hundred li of riverfront.

sentences.zh: 太子劭出鎮石頭，總統水軍，丹楊尹徐湛之守石頭倉城，吏部尚書江湛兼領軍，軍事處置悉以委焉。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Shao went out to garrison Shitou, overall commanding the water army; Danyang Prefect Xu Tanzhi defended Shitou's granary city; Minister of Personnel Jiang Zhan concurrently commanded the army — military dispositions entirely were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Shao took command at Shitou and directed the fleet. Danyang Prefect Xu Tanzhi held the Shitou granary fortress. Minister of Personnel Jiang Zhan acted as commanding general; military affairs were placed entirely in his hands.

sentences.zh: 上登石頭城，有憂色，謂江湛曰：「北伐之計，同議者少。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended Shitou City with a worried look and said to Jiang Zhan: "The northern expedition plan — those who agreed were few.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor climbed Shitou ramparts, his face troubled, and said to Jiang Zhan, "Few counseled this northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 今日士民勞怒，不得無慚。

translations.literal: Today officials and people labor and rage — one cannot be without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Now the people are exhausted and angry. I cannot but feel ashamed.

sentences.zh: 貽大夫之憂，予之過也。」

translations.literal: Causing the great officers' worry — my fault.
translations.idiomatic: I have brought this grief upon the court — it is my fault alone."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「檀道濟若在，豈使胡馬至此？」

translations.literal: Again he said: "If Tan Daoji were alive, how could he allow barbarian horses to reach here?
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "If Tan Daoji were still alive, would barbarian horses have come this far?

sentences.zh: 上又登莫府山，觀望形勢，購魏主及王公首，許以封爵、金帛。

translations.literal: The emperor again ascended Mofu Mountain, observed and surveyed the situation, and offered purchase for the Wei lord's and princes' and dukes' heads — promising enfeoffment rank and gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor climbed Mount Mofu to survey the situation and posted rewards for the heads of the Wei emperor and his princes, promising titles and gold.

sentences.zh: 又募人繼野葛酒置空村中，欲以毒魏人，竟不能傷。

translations.literal: Again he recruited people to steep wild-ge wine and place it in empty villages, wishing to poison Wei people — ultimately could not harm them.
translations.idiomatic: He also had poisoned wine brewed from wild ge and left in deserted villages to kill Wei soldiers, but it did no harm.

sentences.zh: 魏主鑿瓜步山為蟠道，於其上設氈屋。

translations.literal: The Wei lord carved Guabu Mountain into a winding path and on it set felt tents.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor cut a winding road into Mount Guabu and pitched felt pavilions along it.

sentences.zh: 魏主不飲河南水，以橐駝負河北水自隨。

translations.literal: The Wei lord did not drink the south-of-River water; he had camels carry north-of-River water to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: He would not drink water south of the Yellow River and had camels carry water from the north.

sentences.zh: 餉上橐駝、名馬，並求和，請婚。

translations.literal: He sent the emperor camels and famous horses, and jointly sought peace and requested marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Song emperor camels and fine horses, sued for peace, and asked for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 上遣奉朝請田奇餉以珍羞異味。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Attending Courtier Tian Qi to present delicacies and exotic flavors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Attending Courtier Tian Qi with rare delicacies in return.

sentences.zh: 魏主得黃甘，即啖之，並大進酃酒。

translations.literal: The Wei lord obtained yellow citrus and immediately ate it, and greatly advanced Ling wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor ate the oranges at once and sent large quantities of Ling wine.

sentences.zh: 左右有附耳語者，疑食中有毒。

translations.literal: Those at his side whispered in his ear — suspecting poison in the food.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants whispered in his ear, fearing the food was poisoned.

sentences.zh: 魏主不應，舉手指天，以其孫示奇曰：「吾遠來至此，非欲為功名，實欲繼好息民，永結姻援。

translations.literal: The Wei lord did not respond; he raised a finger pointing to Heaven, showed his grandson to Qi and said: "I came from afar to here — not wishing for achievement and fame; truly wishing to continue good relations and rest the people, forever binding marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them, pointed to Heaven, and held up his grandson for Qi to see. "I have come all this way not for glory but to restore peace and bind our houses in marriage.

sentences.zh: 宋若能以女妻此孫，我以女妻武陵王，自今匹馬不復南顧。」

translations.literal: If Song can give a daughter to marry this grandson, I will give a daughter to marry the Prince of Wuling — from now on not a single horse will again look south."
translations.idiomatic: If Song will give this boy a princess, I will give my daughter to Prince of Wuling. Not one horse will cross south again."

sentences.zh: 奇還，上召太子劭及群臣議之。

translations.literal: Qi returned; the emperor summoned Crown Prince Shao and the multitude of ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi returned, the emperor called Crown Prince Shao and the ministers to counsel.

sentences.zh: 眾並謂宜許，江湛曰：「戎狄無親，許之無益。」

translations.literal: The multitude all said it should be granted; Jiang Zhan said: "Barbarians have no kinship — granting it has no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed to accept. Jiang Zhan said, "Barbarians keep no faith. Agreement would do no good.

sentences.zh: 劭怒，謂湛曰：「今三王在厄，詎宜苟執異議！」

translations.literal: Shao angrily said to Zhan: "Now the three princes are in peril — how can one obstinately hold to dissenting views!
translations.idiomatic: Shao flared up and said to him, "Three princes are trapped in the north — how can you cling to dissent!

sentences.zh: 聲色甚厲。

translations.literal: Voice and expression very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: His voice and manner were savage.

sentences.zh: 坐散，俱出，劭使班劍及左右排湛，湛幾至僵仆。

translations.literal: The session dispersed; all went out; Shao had sword guards and those at his side push Zhan — Zhan nearly reached rigid collapse.
translations.idiomatic: When the meeting broke up, Shao's guards shoved Jiang Zhan aside as they left; Zhan nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 劭又言於上曰：「北伐敗辱，數州淪破，獨有斬江湛、徐湛之可以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Shao again spoke to the emperor saying: "The northern expedition's defeat and disgrace — several prefectures lost and broken — only beheading Jiang Zhan and Xu Tanzhi can apologize to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shao told the emperor, "This northern debacle has cost us whole provinces. Only by executing Jiang and Xu can we answer the realm.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「北伐自是我意，江、徐但不異耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The northern expedition was itself my intent — Jiang and Xu only did not differ.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The northern campaign was my own decision. Jiang and Xu merely raised no objection.

sentences.zh: 由是太子與江、徐不平，魏亦竟不成婚。

translations.literal: By this the crown prince and Jiang and Xu were not at peace; Wei also in the end did not achieve marriage.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the crown prince bore a grudge against Jiang and Xu, and the Wei marriage proposal came to nothing.
